papers.sourceText: Q: The tax rebate was a concession given to the civil servants A) a donation B) an allowance C) an incentive D) an emolument. Answer: b Q: We did not understand what the magistrate said about ........ and battery? A) acid B) insult C) assault D) touching Answer: c Q: It is surprising that this politician has now turned renegade? A) milliant B) corrupt C) loyal D) quiet Answer: c Q: The last criticism at the rally was made in ignorance A) uniformed B) objective C) unimpeaccable D) impeccable Answer: a Q: The book described Talle as a? A) The precious child B) The quiet one C) The friendly child D) the holy child Answer: b Q: Tear? . A) dare B) care C) here D) wear Answer: d Solution: The verb tear is pronounced as /tɛː/ Wear is pronounced as /wɛː/ Q: termination? A) terminaTION B) TERmination C) termiNAtion D) terMInation Answer: c Solution: words ending with ''tion are usually stressed on the syllable before the ''tion'' Hence the word will be stressed as ter-mi-NA-tion Q: The invigilator _____ to know how long the examination _____ going on. A) Wanted/ had been. B) Wanted/ has been. C) Want/had been. D) Wanted/have been. Answer: a Solution: The invigilator Wanted to know how long the examination had been going on. Q: A) tear (verb) B) hear C) weird D) mere Answer: c Q: The boys knew that a storm was imminent A) Impending B) encroaching C) possible D) threatening Answer: a Q: sufficiency A) sufFIciency B) SUFficiency C) sufficienCY D) suffiCIENcy Answer: a Q: Thought? A) theatre B) taught C) weather D) fate Answer: a Solution: Both thought and theater are pronounced alike with the tip of the tongue in between the front teeth. Hence we have; thought1; /θɔːt/ theatre;​​​​​​​ /ˈθɪətə/ Q: Everybody is allowed to ………. his views on state matters A) Air B) hear C) show D) share Answer: a Q: The union officials suddenly became reactive A) unruly B) impatient C) calm D) submissive Answer: a Q: Choose the word(s) or phrase(s) which best fill(s) the gap. If it had rained, we would have had to postpone the concert. It didn't rain, so ____________ A) we won't have to B) we would have had to C) we wouldn't have to D) we didn't have to Answer: d Solution: The conditional statement ended with the first sentence. The following statement should therefore end with a past tense Q: We were collectively responsible for keeping the machine in good shape. A) jointly B) severally C) dutifully D) socially. Answer: b Q: This question is from the novel 'The Last Days at Forcados High school'. ‘What is this good-for-nothing doing in my house’. Whose words were these? A) Jimi B) Mrs Solade C) Mr solade D) Wole Answer: c Q: It is important not to let mistakes blight your life A) damage B) impart C) improve D) ruin Answer: c Solution: blight; have a severely detrimental effect on. (a thing that spoils or damages something.) improve; having become or been made better. Q: His comment was not printable A) punishable B) suitable C) offensive D) unfair. Answer: c Q: From what she said, one may infer that she does not like the course A) agree B) deduce C) suppose D) realize Answer: b Q: Always strive to get what is legitimate, A) illicit B) legal C) good D) impure Answer: a Q: The debt the company incurred became rather intolerable. A) inevitable B) unprecedented C) insupportable D) dangerous. Answer: c Q: A) toil B) rejoice C) enjoy D) log Answer: d Q: The weather is probably ..... appealing for people who live in Jos ..... for foreigners? A) as / much as B) more / as C) less / than D) at least as / but Answer: a Q: At the _________ of the century, many ways of doing things were introduced. A) Sight. B) Turn. C) Event. D) Birth. Answer: b Solution: At the turn of the century, many ways of doing things were introduced. Q: As far as Abu is concerned , Mero should be given fifty naira at the most A) All Abu is concerned with is that Mero should be given nothing more than fifty naira B) All Abu is saying is that Mero probably desrves more than fifty naira and not less C) In Abu's estimation, Mero merits not more than fifty naira D) In Abu's opinion, Mero deserves fifty naira or probably more Answer: a Solution: at the most means, not more than. Q: The girl says she is averse.....what others admire A) to B) with C) for D) from Answer: a Solution: 'To'' as an adverb is used here to connect the relationship the speaker and the subject Q: The student BOUGHT the book. A) Who bought the book? B) Did the student steal the book? C) What did the student buy? D) How will the student get the book? Answer: b Q: Joys A) elbow B) pots C) boys D) stays Answer: c Q: suggestible? A) suggeSTIble B) Suggestible C) suGGEstible D) suggestiBLE Answer: c Solution: su-gge-STi-ble

papers.sourceText:
Q: As it relates to sex education, Aliya's father advised that
A)  she should abstain totally from sex as this is the worst sin ever in the history of human civilisation
B) she should wisely decide before letting go of her body
C) she should be mindful of her company of friends and the media's influence on sexual affairs
D) sexual affair is no longer a hidden issue and she should wisely make her choices
Answer: c
Solution: Mr Bello warned Aliya to be careful as regarding the kind of movies, books and progammes she entertain as well the company of friends she keeps.

Q: Both questions are alternatives; you answer ........ one ........ the other
A) either/or
B) neither/nor
C) either/nor
D) neither/or
Answer: a
Solution: Option A is the best answer. Note that 'either' goes with 'or' and the usage of both creates an impression as to alternatives.

Q: The jollof rice served at the wedding reception was [malodorous]
A)  small but palatable
B)  unpalatably big
C) pleasant
D) stale and smelly
Answer: c
Solution: Malodorous is an adjective for an odorous or unpleasant smell.

Q: Aliya's choice of wanting to study medicine …
A) simply reflects her childishness
B)  indicates her affection for humanity
C) is born out of the prospects of the course
D) is primarily because of her father
Answer: b
Solution: Aliya's interest in medicine was just so that she could help asthmatic children in the nearest future by donating inhalers to schools.

Q: In the novel, we learnt that
A) it pays to be diligent and hardworking
B) beauty without character is nothing
C) love and companionship are a no-go-area for teenagers
D)  one should follow the propagation of the media
Answer: b
Solution: Among other things, Aliya's father emphasized that beauty is a relative word and as a matter of fact, beauty without good deeds is all vanity and worthless on the long run. As per dating, the advice is for teenagers to act patiently, this nullifies Option C.

Q: Aliya although is born with a silver spoon, but she has no freedom to move around meet new people unlike other persons. This signals to the…
A) criticism of strict parenting
B) irony of life
C) essence of a child's exposure
D)  expectations of wealthy parents
Answer: b
Solution: Aliya at age 12 envy of the girls hawking on the street and their freedom to move about as compared to her restriction to move about, eventhough she born into a comfortable home, significantly indicates the irony of life i.e no one has it all.

Q: Bolu shall be the M.C. This means that
A) Bolu may be the M.C
B) no one else will be the M.C
C) later in life, Bolu will become an M.C
D) Bolu may not be the M.C
Answer: b
Solution: Shall' indicates a future tense, also 'the M.C' indicates a specific qualification or title. It should be noted that the use of article  'a' is used when we mention something for the first time. However, 'the' is used when something is obvious

Q: 

America is the Mecca of the world
A) America is the commercial garden of the world
B) America is a beautiful place in the world
C) America is a place where people like to visit
D)  America accepts assorted races throughout the world
Answer: c
Solution: The representative quality or title of Mecca indicates here that America is a sought after State by most people to visit

Q: It is high time we ........ seeing her
A) stop
B) will stop
C) stopped
D) stops
Answer: c
Solution: It is high time' suggests that something should be done and that it is already a bit late.

Q: Smoo[th]
A) worth
B) wealthy
C) brother
D) dress
Answer: c
Solution: Brother is the correct answer. The sound present here is pronounceable from the 'TH' in 'these' (not /d/ as in 'drug' or /∅/ as in 'thanks')

Q: Neighb[our]
A) blood
B) standard
C) board
D) source
Answer: b
Solution: The vowel sound obtainable here is the /∂/ sound as in 'brother'. Stand[ar]d qualifies in this regard.

Q: He was both a writer and a politician, but he was better ........ a singer
A) As if
B) Like
C) As
D) to be
Answer: c
Solution: The adverb "as" is the most suitable answer here to govern the noun phrase "a singer".

Q: All in all, Aliya has …
A) the inheritance of her parents both in knowledge and assets
B) been challenged to be exceptional in all her endeavors
C)  the responsibility to pass on the lessons of her father to her own children
D)  been portrayed as the definition of beauty and character
Answer: c
Solution: The most important thing is not only for Aliya to abide by her father's advise built to as well lead such legacies for her children and the generations to come.

Q: Choose the word that has a different stress pattern
A) enlighten
B) unwanted
C) agitate
D) Informal
Answer: c
Solution: The first syllable in 'agitate' is stressed, the other options are stressed differently

Q: Ad[j]ust

Answer: d

The sentence has a singular subject 'it' and a plural subject 'you', hence a plural verb is needed because 'you' is closer.

Q: One challenge associated with presidential system of Government
A) Aim of government
B) separation of power
C) The Senate president
D)  Fusion of power
Answer: b
Solution: A key challenge in a presidential system arises from the separation of powers between the executive and legislature. While designed to prevent tyranny, this separation can lead to gridlock when the president and legislature (controlled by opposing parties) clash over policy, budgets, or appointments. For example, in the U.S., frequent government shutdowns occur due to disagreements between the President and Congress.

Q: Citizenship refers to the
A)  legal status of a member of a state
B) indigenous member of a state
C) highest position in a state
D) social status of a person in a state
Answer: a
Solution: Citizenship refers to the legal recognition of a person as a member of a state. The word "legal" guarantees you the constitutional right to enjoy the benefits of the state.

Q: A form of oligarchy in which gifted people are at the helm of affairs is
A) aristocracy
B) theocracy
C) plutocracy
D) gerontocracy
Answer: a
Solution: Aristocracy refers to a form of government in which power is held by a small, privileged ruling class, typically consisting of individuals who are considered "gifted" or of noble birth. Aristocrats often possess superior social, economic or educational status and are believed to have the qualities necessary to govern effectively.

Theocracy is a form of government in which religious leaders control the government, claiming to be ruling on behalf of a deity. Plutocracy is a system of government where the wealthy class has significant power and influence over political decisions. Gerontocracy is a system where older individuals hold power, often based on age rather than merit or ability.

Q: In the Oyo traditional political system, the Alafin of Oyo was elected or chosen by a group known as
A) Oyo Mesi
B) Bales
C) Obas
D) Ogboni
Answer: a
Solution: In the Oyo Empire’s traditional political system, the Oyo Mesi (a council of seven high-ranking chiefs) held the authority to elect or depose the Alafin. This council ensured checks and balances by selecting a new Alafin from the royal lineage and overseeing his governance.

Q: The main attributes of a state are
A) government, the police and the armed forces
B)  population, territory, government and sovereignty
C) federal state and local governments
D) the press, the legislature, the executive and the judiciary
Answer: b
Solution: The four essential attributes of a state are:

Population: A defined group of people within the state.

Territory: A recognized geographical area with borders.

Government: An organized system to enforce laws and administer policies.

Sovereignty: Supreme authority to govern without external interference.

Q: Nigeria spearheaded the formation of ECOWAS during the regime of
A) Olusegun Obasanjo
B) Yakubu Gowon
C) Muritala Muhammad
D) Ibrahim Babangida
Answer: b
Solution: Nigeria played a pivotal role in the formation of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) during the regime of General Yakubu Gowon. In collaboration with Togolese President Gnassingbé Eyadéma, Gowon initiated efforts to promote economic integration in West Africa. Their joint diplomatic missions across the region culminated in the signing of the Treaty of Lagos on May 28, 1975, officially establishing ECOWAS. ​

Q: A good example of a country with a largely unwritten constitution is
A) the United States of America
B) The Soviet Union
C) Nigeria
D) United Kingdom
Answer: d
Solution: The United Kingdom operates under an uncodified constitution, often referred to as an "unwritten" constitution. This means that, unlike countries with a single, consolidated constitutional document, the UK's constitutional framework is derived from multiple sources, including statutes, common law, conventions, and historical documents. While many elements are written, they are not compiled into a single document, distinguishing the UK from nations with codified constitutions

Q: A referendum is a device to ensure that
A) elections are free and fair
B) legislators vote to resolve contentious issues
C)  decisions are effected with the consent of citizens
D) bye-elections are held to fill vacant positions
Answer: c
Solution: A referendum is a direct voting process in which the electorate is invited to vote on a particular proposal and decide on issues such as constitutional amendments, changes in laws, or specific policies. This process ensures that decisions reflect the will of the citizens, as it requires their direct approval or disapproval. Unlike regular elections, which select representatives, referendums allow citizens to have a say on specific legislative or policy issues directly.

Q: Who was the political head of the Old Oyo Empire?
A) Bashorun
B) Oyomesi
C) Aremo
D) Alaafin
Answer: d
Solution: This position is regarded as sacred and spirit being. So the Alafin is regarded as the spiritual head of the Oyo kingdom.

Q: An electoral process in which candidates are selected for elective offices by party members is
A) primary election
B) electoral college
C) bye election
D) general election
Answer: a
Solution: It is only the party that can nominate (choose) an individual for a position or post. Furthermore, it an in-house affair where the party’s candidate is given a ticket to vote for a particular post.

Q: A state that is ruled by an elected citizen is
A) a republic
B) a plutocracy
C) a monarchy
D) an empire
Answer: a
Solution: Republic is defined as a situation or process whereby the people democratically elect their leaders into public or political offices.

Q: Which of these rulers resisted colonial rule and was deported to Calabar?
A) King Kosoko
B)  King Dosunmu
C) Oba Ovonramwen
D) King Jaja
Answer: c
Solution: In February 1897, the British colonial forces invaded and conquered Benin City. Oba Ovoranmwen was dethroned, and deported to calabar where he lived and died in the month of January 1914, after sixteen years of British captivity. He was later buried at old Calabar by official of colonial authority in the absence of his Benin royal family.

Q: The act of removing an elected official by the electorate is referred to as
A) impeachment
B) consensus
C) recall
D) plebiscite
Answer: c
Solution: A recall is a procedure that allows voters to remove an elected official from office before their term is completed. This process is initiated by the electorate, and if sufficient signatures or support is gathered, a recall election is held. This is distinct from impeachment, which is a legislative process used to remove officials from office for misconduct, and from plebiscite, which is a direct vote by the electorate on an important public question.

Q: The following are international organisations except
A) pressure group
B) O.A.U
C) U.N.O.
D) Commonwealth of nations
Answer: a
Solution: International organizations are typically formal institutions where multiple countries cooperate to achieve common goals. Examples include the Organization of African Unity (now the African Union), the United Nations Organization (UNO), and the Commonwealth of Nations, which involve governments coming together to coordinate policies and address global or regional issues. In contrast, a pressure group is an interest group that seeks to influence government policy and decision-making but is not an international organization in the formal, intergovernmental sense.

Q: Under a presidential system of government, the legislature and the executive are
A) elected separately to an unfixed term
B)  appointed at the same time to an unfixed term
C) appointed by the judiciary to a fixed term
D) elected separately to a fixed term
Answer: d
Solution: In a presidential system of government, the executive and legislative branches are distinct and independent from each other. Both the president (executive) and the members of the legislature are elected separately by the populace. Additionally, they serve fixed terms in office, meaning their tenure is predetermined and not subject to arbitrary dismissal by the other branch. This structure ensures a clear separation of powers and a system of checks and balances between the branches.

Q: The term, rule of law means
A) nobody is above the law
B) everybody is equal before the law
C) we are being governed by lawyers
D)  A and B above
Answer: d
Solution: The term "rule of law" embodies the principles that:​

Nobody is above the law: All individuals, regardless of status or position, are subject to the law. ​

Everybody is equal before the law: Every person is entitled to equal treatment under the law, ensuring fairness and justice without discrimination.

Q: Which of these is not the supreme organ of the OAU?
A) The Council of Ministers
B) The Administrative Secretary General
C)  The Assembly of Heads of States and Government
D) Appointment of staff
Answer: d
Solution: The Organization of African Unity (OAU) had several principal organs, including:​

The Assembly of Heads of State and Government: The supreme decision-making body of the OAU.​

The Council of Ministers: Composed of foreign ministers or designated representatives from member states, responsible for preparing conferences and implementing decisions of the Assembly.​

The General Secretariat: Headed by the Administrative Secretary-General, responsible for coordinating the activities of the OAU.

Q: In which of the following systems is the power of the component units more than that of the central government?
A) Monarchical
B) Federal Governments
C) Unitary
D) Confederal
Answer: d
Solution: In a confederal system, the component units (such as states or regions) possess more authority than the central government. This arrangement allows the constituent entities to retain their sovereignty and delegate only specific, limited powers to the central authority, often related to common interests like defense or foreign affairs. Consequently, the central government operates at the behest of the component units and lacks independent authority. 

Q: Federalism was introduced in Nigeria under the
A) Lyttelton Constitution
B) Macpherson Constitution
C) Richards Constitution
D)  Independence
Answer: a
Solution: The Lyttleton Constitution was enacted in 1954 and it established the federal system of government and paved the way for independence.

This constitution is considered the start of federalism, as it provided for a division of power between the central government and the regions, unlike the Richards constitution that created provinces/regions, with no autonomy being given to the regions.

Q: When a bill passed by legislature is vetoed by the executive, the action underscores the principle of
A) collective responsibility
B)  probity and accountability
C) checks and balances
D) separation of powers
Answer: c
Solution: When the executive branch vetoes a bill passed by the legislature, it exemplifies the principle of checks and balances. This system ensures that no single branch of government becomes too powerful by granting each branch specific powers to limit the actions of the others. In this case, the executive's veto power serves as a check on the legislative branch, preventing the enactment of legislation without executive approval. Conversely, the legislative branch can override a presidential veto with a two-thirds majority in both houses, maintaining a balance of power between the branches

Q: The main role of pressure groups is to
A)  influence the legislature to make decision favourable to them
B) inject emotion and selfish debates
C)  influence the public
D) use all means, including bribery, to achieve their objectives
Answer: a
Solution: The primary role of pressure groups is to advocate for specific policies or interests by influencing legislators and policymakers. They achieve this through lobbying, submitting proposals, organizing campaigns, and testifying at hearings. For example, environmental groups push for climate legislation, while trade unions advocate for labor rights.

Q: France introduced the policy of assimilation in her colonies primarily to
A)  teach them the art of leadership
B) give them a sound education
C) change their way of life
D) discourage them from ritual killings
Answer: c
Solution: The French policy of assimilation was designed to transform the cultural identities of colonized peoples by encouraging them to adopt French language, customs, and laws. The underlying goal was to integrate colonial subjects into French society, effectively changing their traditional ways of life to mirror that of France. This approach was rooted in the belief that spreading French civilization would "civilize" the colonies, leading to the erosion of indigenous cultures and practices.

Q: Which of these constitutions recognised local government as a third tier of government in Nigeria?
A) 1960 Constitution
B) 1963 Constitution
C) 1979 Constitution
D) 1946 Constitution
Answer: c
Solution: The 1979 Constitution of Nigeria recognised local government as the third tier of government. This was a significant development in Nigeria's constitutional history, as it formalised the structure and functions of local governments, granting them autonomy and recognition alongside the federal and state governments. The earlier constitutions, such as the 1960 and 1963 constitutions, did not provide for local governments as a distinct tier, and the 1946 Constitution primarily focused on colonial administration without recognizing local governments in this way.

Q: n the Presidential System of Government, the president is elected to office by
A) the Cabinet
B) the Parliament or Legislature
C) Military
D) the people through direct elections
Answer: d
Solution: In a Presidential System of Government, the president is elected to office by the people through direct elections. This means that citizens have the opportunity to vote directly for their president, rather than the president being appointed or elected by the legislature, cabinet or military. 

Q: The OAU was formed in
A) 1946
B) 1956
C) 1960
D) 1963
Answer: d
Solution: The Organisation of African Unity (OAU) was formed on May 25, 1963, in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. It was established to promote unity and cooperation among African countries and to support the decolonization of African nations. It was later replaced by the African Union (AU) in 2001 to address more modern political and economic challenges.

Q: The dominant idea behind the establishment of the Organization of African Unity is
A) that Africa must unite
B) to show the world that Africa can also do what Latin American and Asian countries have done
C) to provide a framework and opportunities for co-operation on common African problems
D) to promote economic development of Africa
Answer: a
Solution: It is a forum to unite Africa and eradicate colonialism and imperialism.

Q: How many states were created in Nigeria in 1967?
A) 4
B) 12
C) 19
D) 21
Answer: b
Solution: In 1967, Nigeria was reorganized from four regions into 12 states by General Yakubu Gowon. This move was designed to reduce ethnic tensions, promote administrative efficiency, and weaken regional power bases that had contributed to the country's political instability.

Q: Before Nigeria became a republic, the highest body charged with the administration of justice was the
A) Supreme Court
B)  Court of Appeal
C) Privy Court
D) High Court
Answer: c
Solution: Before Nigeria became a republic in 1963, the highest judicial authority was the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council in the United Kingdom. During this period, decisions from Nigeria's Federal Supreme Court could be appealed to the Privy Council, which served as the final court of appeal for British colonies and certain Commonwealth countries

Q: A constitution that requires a plebiscite or a referendum to be amended is
A) written
B) flexible
C) rigid
D) unwritten
Answer: c
Solution: A rigid constitution requires a special procedure (e.g., a plebiscite, referendum, or supermajority legislative vote) for amendment, distinguishing it from ordinary laws. This design protects fundamental principles from frequent or hasty changes.

Q: The Mid-Western Region was created in Nigeria in
A) 1961
B) 1962
C) 1963
D) 1964
Answer: c
Solution: The Mid-Western Region was created in Nigeria on August 9, 1963. It was established as a result of the 1962 census and was the first new region to be created in Nigeria after independence. This change was part of a broader effort to accommodate Nigeria's diverse ethnic and cultural groups in the federal structure.

Q: In the history of Nigeria, 1914 was the
A) year the British established their rule over Nigeria
B) beginning of first world war
C) year Lugard effected amalgamation of Nigeria
D) year the railway system was completed
Answer: c
Solution: In 1914, the British colonial administrator Lord Frederick Lugard merged the Northern and Southern protectorates to form the single colony of Nigeria. This amalgamation was a significant event in Nigerian history, as it established the framework for the modern state of Nigeria under British colonial rule.

Q: In a Federal System (such as Nigeria) the Local Governments are directly responsible
A) to the Federal or Central Government
B)  to the State Government
C)  to the Federal and State Government
D) to no other level of government
Answer: b
Solution: n Nigeria’s federal system, local governments are established and administered by the state governments. Although they may receive funding or guidance from the federal level, their direct accountability and oversight come from the state government rather than the federal or central government.

Q: The system of indirect rule failed in the former Eastern Nigeria primarily because
A) of the fragmented political structures
B)  the Chief refused to cooperate with colonial officers
C) the high incidence of taxation Chief refused to cooperate with colonial officers
D) the colonial officers imposed warrant chiefs on the people
Answer: a
Solution: Indirect rule depended on the existence of centralized traditional authorities who could effectively serve as intermediaries between the colonial government and the local populace. In Eastern Nigeria, however, the political landscape was characterized by highly fragmented, decentralized communities without a strong, unified leadership structure. This made it difficult for the British colonial administration to implement its indirect rule policies effectively, as there was no single traditional authority to coordinate and enforce colonial directives across the region.

Q: The Igbo political system was based on
A) Age Grades
B) Umunna
C) Family ties
D) Umuada
Answer: b
Solution: The Igbo pre-colonial political system was fundamentally decentralized and based on kinship structures, with the Umunna serving as the primary unit of political organization. The Umunna refers to a patrilineal kinship group or extended family unit, consisting of individuals who share a common male ancestor. Each Umunna was led by the eldest male, known as the Diokpala, who, along with other elders, played a significant role in decision-making and governance within the community. This structure ensured that authority was distributed among various family heads, fostering a republican and egalitarian society

Q: The rights of a citizen can be withdrawn by the state if the person
A) opposes the government violently
B)  leave the country permanently
C)  is convicted of a serious crime
D) is pronounced dead
Answer: c
Solution: In many constitutional democracies, while citizens generally enjoy a wide range of rights, these rights can be curtailed in certain circumstances. One common legal provision is that upon conviction of a serious crime, certain rights (such as the right to vote or hold public office) may be withdrawn or limited for the duration of the sentence or as stipulated by law.

Q: The two leaders that played the most prominent roles in the formation of the ECOWAS were
A) Gowon and Eyadema
B) Kountche and Senghor
C) Kerekou and Tubman
D) Acheampong and Jawara
Answer: a
Solution: Both Leaders (Gen. Yakubu Gowon of Nigeria and Eyadema of Togo) used their military might to facilitate the organization.

Q: Nigeria’s quest for a leadership role in Africa hinges principally on her
A) military might
B) size and population
C) generosity
D) economic strength
Answer: b
Solution: Nigeria’s size and population is a credit which makes other African countries take refuge in it. Beside, Nigeria’s role in handling other African issues (i.e ) internal crises, attention to natural disaster e t c is second to none .

Q: A major function of Warrant Chiefs was to
A) take charge of local administration
B) stop ritual killings
C) prevent tribal wars
D) supervise native courts and markets
Answer: a
Solution: Under the colonial system of indirect rule in Nigeria, warrant chiefs were appointed by the British colonial authorities to serve as intermediaries between the colonial government and the indigenous communities. Their primary function was to manage local administration, including tax collection, maintenance of order, and implementation of colonial policies, thus ensuring that the colonial government’s interests were maintained at the local level.

Q: One of the principal objectives of the OPEC is to
A) determine oil prices in the international market
B) harmonise the oil policies of member countries
C) discipline erring oil-producing countries
D) assist non-oil producing developing states
Answer: b
Solution: One of the principal objectives of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) is to harmonise and coordinate the oil production policies of its member countries. This coordination helps to stabilise oil markets and ensure fair and stable prices for petroleum producers while securing a reliable supply for consumers. While OPEC does have some influence over oil prices in the international market (option A), its primary focus is on aligning the policies of its member states to achieve mutual benefits rather than directly setting prices

Q: Which of the following world powers was the first to come to Nigeria’s aid during the civil war?
A) Germany
B) USA
C) USSR
D) UK
Answer: d
Solution: During the Nigerian Civil War (1967–1970), Britain was the first world power to come to Nigeria's aid. They supported the Federal Government's military efforts. This support was largely driven by political, economic, and strategic interests, including the desire to maintain relations with Nigeria as a former colony and the geopolitical situation during the Cold War.

Q: Delegated legislation is the—
A) limitation of responsibilities to agencies
B) transfer of responsibilities to agencies
C) deterring of responsibilities of agencies
D) facilitation responsibilities of agencies.
Answer: b
Solution: Delegated legislation involves transferring legislative powers to other bodies.

Q: In 1987, Nigeria attained a federation of __
A) 19 states
B)   12 states
C) 21 states
D) 30 states.
Answer: c
Solution: In 1987, Nigeria had 21 states.

Q: Activities of pressure groups that influence governmental decisions are hampered by __
A) its size
B) its leadership
C)  its affiliation
D) the economy.
Answer: d
Solution: Economic conditions can significantly impact the activities of pressure groups.

Q: Which of the following countries significantly contributed to the formation of ECOMOG?
A) Ghana
B) Gambia
C) Liberia
D) Nigeria
Answer: d
Solution: Nigeria played a major role in the formation and operations of ECOMOG.

Q: Which of the following Nigerian president initiated and facilitated the creation of NEPAD?
A) Goodluck Jonathan
B) Olusegun Obasanjo
C) Umaru Musa Yar'dua
D) Mohammadu Buhari
Answer: b
Solution: Former President Obasanjo played a key role in the creation of NEPAD.

Q: Bills passed by the legislature usually requires the approval of the following except_______
A) Governor
B)  Member house of representative
C) Monarch
D) President
Answer: b
Solution: A bill is usually considered and voted on by members of the House of Representatives, but it does not require their approval again after being passed. The bill must go through a formal process that involves both chambers of the legislature and then requires the executive's approval.

In a federal system like that of the United States or Nigeria, a bill passed by the national legislature (e.g., Congress or the National Assembly) requires the president's assent to become law. Also, in many countries, especially in federal systems like Nigeria, a bill passed by the state legislature requires the governor's assent to become law. In some countries with a constitutional monarchy, such as the United Kingdom, bills require royal assent from the monarch.

Q: The popularity of a political party in given democracy rests on its __
A) constitution
B) manifesto
C) ideology
D)  number of branches.
Answer: b
Solution: A political party's popularity depends largely on its manifesto, which outlines its vision and policies.

Q: In the pre-colonial Emirate system, the emir of Gwandu controlled the __
A) Central section
B) Southern section
C) Eastern section
D)  Western section.
Answer: d
Solution:  In the Emirate system, the Emir of Gwandu controlled the western section.

Q: Nigeria became a republic with the __
A) 1979 Constitution
B) 1989 Constitution
C) 1960 Constitution
D) 1963 Constitution.
Answer: d
Solution: Nigeria became a republic under the 1963 Constitution (though the 1960 Constitution led to independence).

Q: The granting of internal authority to the regions came under which constitution?
A) Littleton Constitution
B) Richard Constitution
C) Clifford Constitution
D) Macpherson Constitution
Answer: b
Solution: This constitution was the only constitution that granted Internal authority

Q: The Ombudsman aims at ___
A) offering qualitative educational services
B) rendering alternative dispute resolution services
C)  providing qualitative job opportunities
D) entertaining complaints on abuse of public office.
Answer: d
Solution: The Ombudsman addresses complaints regarding the misuse of public office.

Q: In the year 1911, who argued most representative system deteriorates towards an Oligarchy or Patriarchy?
A) Robert Michels
B)  Adolf Gasser
C) Adolf Hitler
D) Edmunde Burke
Answer: a
Solution: He is the author of the book "Political Parties" argues that most representative systems deteriorates towards an Oligarchy or Patriarchy in the year 1911

Q: The concentration of power on the units is a merit of __
A)  quasi-federal-system
B) confederal system
C)  federal system

D) system
Answer: b
Solution: In a confederation, power is concentrated at the unit level.

Q: Nigeria's action towards the external environment is embedded in her ___
A) state policy
B) party policy
C) government policy
D) foreign policy.
Answer: d
Solution: A country's interaction with other nations is guided by its foreign policy. Nigeria’s foreign policy dictates its diplomatic, economic, and political relations with other countries and international organizations.

Q: The political achievement of UN is the promotion of ___
A) economic development
B) educational development
C)  international peace and security
D) democratic institution.
Answer: c
Solution: The UN's primary political achievement is maintaining international peace and security.

Q: A major objective of Public Complaints Commission is __
A) creating fair opportunities for all government employees
B)  training and promoting public servants

C) addressing grievances of individuals and groups
D) creating an efficient work environment.
Answer: c
Solution: The Public Complaints Commission deals with individual and group grievances.

Q: Development of the Civil Service relies on __
A) impartiality
B) anonymity
C) pro notability
D) neutrality
Answer: d
Solution: The development of the civil service relies on its ability to remain neutral.

Q:  Elective principle in Nigeria was first introduced by __
A) Richards Constitution
B) Macpherson Constitution
C) Littleton Constitution
D) Clifford Constitution.
Answer: d
Solution: The elective principle was first introduced in Nigeria by the Clifford Constitution of 1922.

Q: Which of the following is the oldest Public Corporation in Nigeria?
A) Power Distribution Company of Nigeria
B) Nigeria Mining Corporation
C) Nigerian Railway Corporation
D) Nigerian Postal Services.
Answer: c
Solution: Established in 1898, it is the oldest public corporation in Nigeria.


Q:  In fascism, the leader is __
A) supreme
B) democratic
C) rich
D) religious
Answer: a
Solution: In fascism, the leader holds absolute power.

Q: Both federal and state governments derive power from the __
A) residual list
B) concurrent list
C) exclusive list
D) regional list.
Answer: b
Solution: Both federal and state governments share powers from the concurrent list.

Q: In the 18th century, a new wind of development blew over Europe and the development was referred to__________?
A) Labour Revolution
B) Doctrine Revolution
C) Industrial Revolution
D) Economic Revolution
Answer: c
Solution: Industrial revolution came into existence and there was a change in the means of production and domestic system of manufacturing

Q: One major merit of the Unitary system of government is that_______?
A) is most democratic
B) is cheaper to operate
C) eradicates co-operation
D)  eliminate tyranny
Answer: b
Solution: It is cheaper to operate because unitary system of government is a system of government in which power is concentrated in a single system

Q: The head of government under the 1979 Constitution is the _____
A) president
B)  prime minister
C) speaker of the house of represenative
D) senate president
Answer: a
Solution: Nigeria became a federal republic under the Constitution of 1963 and the monarch and Governor-General were replaced by a ceremonial President. In 1979, under the 1979 Constitution, the President gained executive powers, becoming head of both state and government.

Q: The struggle for self- government from foreign rule is known as __
A) imperialism
B) nationalism
C) patriotism
D) neo-colonialism.
Answer: b
Solution: Nationalism refers to the struggle for self-government from foreign rule.

Q: A social group consisting of two or more people who interact and identify will one another is __
A) nation
B) society
C) government
D) state
Answer: b
Solution: A society consists of individuals who interact and identify with one another.

Q: A system of local council that allows for rotational leadership is known as __
A) single executive
B) dual executive
C) multi executive
D) collegiate executive.
Answer: d
Solution: A collegiate executive system allows for rotational leadership.

Q: The Constitutional forms with two levels of Government is _________
A) unitary
B) Evolution
C) Confederal
D) Confederation
Answer: d
Solution: Confederation is the Constitutional form with the levels of Government, the Central and the Regional

Q: Which of the following is a merit of aristocracy?
A) Leaders must have military experience
B)  The best citizen is in control of government
C) Organised few control the government
D)  Majority control the government.
Answer: b
Solution: The best citizen is in control of government – Aristocracy is a system where governance is by the most qualified individuals.


Q: An important element of the doctrine of separation of powers is __
A) Delegation of power
B)  Checks and Balances
C) Rule of Law
D) Concentration diffusion of powers.
Answer: b
Solution: The doctrine of separation of powers ensures that the three branches of government (executive, legislative, and judiciary) operate independently. However, to prevent abuse of power, each branch has mechanisms to check and balance the powers of the others.

Q: Shortage of trained personnel is a major problem of the __
A)  Federal Government
B)  State Governments
C) Regional Governments
D) Local Governments.
Answer: d
Solution:  Local governments often struggle with a lack of trained personnel.

Q: Which of the following is a foremost right of a citizen?
A) Religious right
B) Academic right
C) Right to life
D) Private life.
Answer: c
Solution: The right to life is a fundamental human right that all citizens are entitled to.

Q: Which of the following is a major feature of democracy?
A) Capacity to influence people
B)  Existence of political office holders
C)  Decision making
D) Consent of the people.
Answer: d
Solution: Democracy is based on the consent of the governed.

Q:  Which of the following is a function of the civil service commission?
A) Enforcement of law and order
B) Payment of civil servants salaries
C)  Discipline of erring civil servants
D) Pro action of lives and properties.
Answer: c
Solution: The Civil Service Commission is responsible for maintaining discipline within the civil service.

Q:  To facilitate the effective achievement of its objectives, ECOWAS is operationally structured with ___
A) councils
B) panels
C) committees
D) commissions
Answer: d
Solution:  ECOWAS operates through commissions to achieve its objectives effectively.

Q: Territorial defence in the Yoruba pre-colonial system was the responsibility of the __
A) Bashorun
B) Oyomesi
C) Aremo
D) Are-Ona-Kakanfo
Answer: d
Solution: The Are-Ona-Kakanfo was responsible for territorial defense in the Yoruba pre-colonial system.

Q:  The right of a state is known as ___
A) authority
B) power
C) sovereignty
D) legitimacy
Answer: c
Solution:  Sovereignty refers to the supreme authority of a state.

Q: The essence of ECOWAS is to________
A) bring political parties together
B) foster interstate economic and political co-operation
C) emerging political event
D) expansion of scopes and powers
Answer: b
Solution: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is a regional organisation of 15 West African countries established on 28 May 1975. Its main goal is the promotion of the economic integration among its members. Indeed, ECOWASis one the five regional pillars of the African Economic Community (AEC).

Q: One of the problems of the Commonwealth of Nations is lack of __
A) finance
B)  administrative structures
C)  cultural heterogeneity
D) capacity to enforce decisions.
Answer: d
Solution: The Commonwealth lacks the power to enforce its decisions.

Q: Universal Adult Suffrage permits all __
A) citizens to vote
B)  qualified male to vote
C) qualified citizens to vote
D) female to vote.
Answer: c
Solution: Universal adult suffrage allows all qualified citizens, regardless of gender, to vote.

papers.sourceText:
Q: A rigid constitution is a feature of
A) unitary system
B) monarchical system
C) federal system
D)  confederal system
Answer: c
Solution:  Federal systems typically have rigid constitutions to maintain power separation between levels of government.

Q: The limitation of the right to life can be found
A)  among the people
B) in the case of a convicted person
C) n the executive
D) in the government.
Answer: b
Solution: The right to life may be limited for convicted criminals under capital punishment laws.

Q: n democracies, the political participation could be restricted on the basis of
A) religion
B) age
C) sex
D) class
Answer: b
Solution: Political participation is restricted based on age, as there are voting and candidacy age limits.

Q: In 1973, following an OAU resolution, Nigeria broke diplomatic relations with
A) South Africa
B) France
C) lsreal
D) Cuba
Answer: c
Solution: Nigeria cut diplomatic ties with Israel in 1973 following an OAU resolution over the Yom Kippur War.

Q: Democracy can be promoted through
A) gerrymandering
B) slander
C) accountability
D) lobbying
Answer: c
Solution: Democracy is strengthened through government accountability to the people.

Q: In 1993, Nigerian troops were on peace-keeping assignment to
A) Liberia and Burundi
B) Rwanda and liberia
C) Chad and Liberia
D) Liberia and somalia
Answer: d
Solution: Nigerian troops were actively involved in peace-keeping missions in both Liberia and Somalia in 1993. In Liberia, they were part of the Economic Community of West African States Monitoring Group (ECOMOG), which aimed to restore peace during the Liberian Civil War. In Somalia, Nigerian troops were part of the United Nations Operation in Somalia II (UNOSOM II), which sought to stabilise the country amidst civil unrest.

Q: A.V. Dicey popularised the principle of
A) rule of law
B) democracy
C) political vulture
D) separation of powers
Answer: a
Solution: A.V. Dicey is known for popularizing the rule of law concept.

Q: An alien who has lived in Nigeria for twenty years may acquire citizenship by
A) nationalisation
B) naturalization
C) registration
D) marriage
Answer: b
Solution: An alien who has lived in Nigeria for many years can acquire citizenship through naturalization.

Q: The major liberation organisation which fought for Namibia's independence was
A) SWAPO
B) ANC
C) FRELIMO
D) M.P.L.A
Answer: a
Solution: The South West Africa People’s Organization (SWAPO) fought for Namibia’s independence.

Q: A system of government where political powers are inherited is called
A) monarchy
B) diarchy
C) democracy
D) aristocracy
Answer: a
Solution: A monarchy is a system where political power is inherited.

Q: Which of the following did not generate political crisis in Nigeria?
A) Adoption of Abuja as the New Federal General Elections Capital
B)  Motion for self government in 1956 by Enahoro
C) 1965 election in the Western Region
D) 1964 General Elections
Answer: a
Solution: While other events caused political crises, Abuja’s adoption did not.

Q: Power refers to the__________
A) ability to impose one’s will upon others
B)  duties an individual imposes on himself
C) legal nature of a constitution
D) duties political parties demand of their registered members
Answer: a
Solution: Power is referred to as the ability to control others by imposing ones will on others

Q: Nigeria's foreign policy of non-alignment was a reaction to
A) British imperialism
B)  East-West ideological competition
C) militarism of ex-colonial powers
D) World poverty.
Answer: b
Solution: Nigeria’s non-alignment policy was to avoid taking sides in the Cold War between the USA and USSR.

Q: Political sovereignty belongs to
A)  the people
B) government
C) military
D) the parliament
Answer: a
Solution: In a democracy, political sovereignty rests with the people.

Q: Unicameral legislatures are popular in
A) unitary system
B) federal system
C) confederal
D)  rigid system
Answer: a
Solution: Unicameral legislatures (having only one legislative chamber) are common in unitary systems, where power is centralized, and there is no need for a second chamber to represent different regions or states, as in a federal system.








Q: Which organ of government is vested with the responsibility of initiating bills and recommending them to the legislature for consideration?
A) Federal House of Representatives
B) Executive
C) Senate
D) Judiciary
Answer: b
Solution: The executive arm initiates bills and presents them to the legislature for consideration.

Q: Which of the following was the first political party in Nigeria?
A) The Action Group (AG)
B) Northern People's Congress (NPC)
C) National Council of Nigeria and the Camerouns (NCNC)
D) Nigerian National Democratic Party (NNDP)
Answer: d
Solution: The NNDP, founded in 1923 by Herbert Macaulay, was Nigeria's first political party.

Q: One major achievement of the Richards Constitution of Nigeria was that it
A) united the North and South under a single legislature
B) provided for official African members of the Executive Council
C)  allowed the participation of traditional rulers in government
D)  introduced the elective principle.
Answer: a
Solution: The Richards Constitution (1946) brought the North and South together under a unified legislative framework.

Q: A country is most likely to have a good government only if it has
A) a good constitution but bad operators
B)  good operators but bad constitution
C) a good constitution and good operators
D) illegitimate government.
Answer: c
Solution: A good government requires both a sound legal framework (constitution) and competent leaders (operators).

Q: Which of the following is not an agent of political socialisation?
A) Tourism
B) Mass media
C)  Peer group
D) University
Answer: a
Solution: Tourism is not an agent of political socialization, unlike media, peers, and educational institutions.

Q: Which of these international organisations is the predecessor of the United Nations?
A)  The European Economic Community
B) The organisation of American Statess
C) The League of Nations.
D) The North Atlantic Treaty Organisation
Answer: c
Solution: The United Nations (UN) was formed in 1945 as a successor to the League of Nations.

Q: The second ballot is based on the principle that a successful candidate must obtain
A) absolute majority
B) simple majority
C) forty percent of the votes
D) fifty percent of the votes
Answer: a
Solution: Before the Second Ballot System is introduce in an election is when none of the candidates wins the election by absolute majority in a general election, another election would be conducted. In this final election, only the candidates with the highest votes are allowed to contest. 

So the second ballot is based on the principle that a successful candidate must obtain Absolute Majority

Absolute Majority System is a system of voting in which a candidate must acquire more than half of the total vote cast before he can be declared winner.

Q: An Agency of the united Nations which specializes in the welfare of children is the _______
A) WHO
B) UNESCO
C) UNICEF
D) UNDP
Answer: c
Solution: UNICEF is an agency of UNO that deals and specializes in the welfare, education and needs of children all over the world

Q: Delegated legislation is suitable for
A) relieving the parliament of its workload
B)  enthroning the rule of law
C) ensuring the fusion of powers
D) checking the executive arm of government.
Answer: a
Solution: Delegated legislation allows the executive and agencies to make laws under parliamentary supervision.

Q: A representative government can be established through
A) a general election
B) a military coup
C) apartheid
D) espionage
Answer: a
Solution: Representative government is established through elections.

Q: Which of the following is a basic principle of democracy? Rule by
A) the majority and the right of the minority
B)  the minority at the expense of the majority
C) the wealthy few
D) two political parties.
Answer: a
Solution: Democracy ensures majority rule while protecting minority rights.

Q:  The first Head of State and Head of Government in Nigeria was
A)  Lord Fredick Lugard
B) Alhaji Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
C) General J.T.U. Aguiyi Ironsi
D)  Alhaji Shehu Shagari
Answer: c
Solution: He became Nigeria’s first Head of State after the 1966 coup.

Q: The primary function of government in a state is to ___
A) build schools and hospitals
B) provide transport services
C) engage in campaigns and rallies
D) maintain law and order.
Answer: d
Solution:  The primary function of government is to ensure law and order, creating a stable society.

Q: The creation of more states in Nigeria has_______

A) eliminated ethnic and religious conflicts
B) reduced the gap between the rich and poor states
C) increased the powers of the federal government
D) increased the powers of the states and local government
Answer: a
Solution: The creation of more states in Nigeria has eliminated ethnic and religious conflicts which used to be a bane of crises in the country, as both minor and major ethnic groups are involved.

Q: Legitimacy is determined mainly by
A) charisma
B) influence
C) acceptance
D) desire
Answer: c
Solution: Legitimacy is determined by the people's acceptance of a government’s rule.

Q: Disenfranchisement refers to the
A) qualification of voters in an election
B) Disqualification of fraudulent president aspirants
C) denial of the right to vote in an election
D) right to vote and be voted for.
Answer: c
Solution: Disenfranchisement means being deprived of voting rights.

Q: Which of the following is the lowest in the hierarchy of feudal system?
A) Knights
B) Serfs
C) Nobles
D) Lords
Answer: b
Solution: Serfs were the lowest class in the feudal system.

Q: Political authority is vested in the_________
A) state
B) judiciary
C) government
D) armed forces
Answer: c
Solution: Political Authority is the authority conferred on a persons holding political offices, e.g the president, legislators etc. and the president, legislator and others are considered to be the Government

So Political authority is vested in the Government

Q:  Which of the following countries had a strained relationship with Nigeria over the Angolan crisis of 1975?
A) The Soviet Union
B) Tanzania
C) The United States of America
D) South Africa
Answer: c
Solution: Nigeria opposed U.S. policy on the Angolan crisis, as Nigeria supported the MPLA while the U.S. backed UNITA.

Q: An important aspect of an unwritten constitution is that it
A)  is easy to understand to everybody
B) safeguards the monarchy
C) contains customary laws and conventions
D) is not easily amended
Answer: c
Solution: An unwritten constitution refers to when the whole body of fundamental laws, customs, conventions, principles, rules and regulations according to which a particular government of a country operates are not written down or codified in a single document.

An important aspect of an unwritten constitution is that it contains customary laws and conventions

Q: The tenure of the president of the UN Security Council is
A) one month
B)  six months
C) two years
D) one year
Answer: a
Solution: The Security Council is one of the organs of U.N.O and it is assumed to be the most powerful of all the organs, making up the organization. Formerly, it was made up of 5 permanent members also known as the Permanent Five, Big Five, or P5 and 6 non-permanent members, but it was enlarged in 1965, bringing 6 non-permanent members to 10, making it 15 members. The permanent members are: United States of America (USA), China, Britain, France and Russia. 

The President of the United Nations Security Council is the presiding officer of that body. The President is the head of the delegation from the United Nations Security Council member state that holds the rotating presidency for a tenure of One Month. the presidency rotates monthly among the state members of the Security Council. The rotation takes place in alphabetical order of the member states' official United Nations names in English

Q: Nationalism in Africa eventually led to
A)  a rapid political awareness among the colonialists
B) the alignment of the new states
C) de-colonisation
D)  international economic groupings.
Answer: c
Solution: African nationalism led to independence from colonial rule.

Q: Between 1960 and 1980, Nigeria experienced all the following systems of government except
A) unitary
B) federal
C) confederal
D) parliamentary
Answer: c
Solution: Nigeria has never operated a confederal system of government, only federal, unitary (briefly during military rule), and parliamentary systems.

Q: The indirect rule system succeeded in the Hausa-Fulani society because the
A)  A society had only one religion
B)  people received Quranic education
C) people were descendants of Uthman dan Fodio
D) existing administration favoured the system.
Answer: d
Solution: The Hausa-Fulani traditional system had a strong hierarchical structure that suited indirect rule.

Q: The policy of Association was adopted by the.
A)  British to replace their policy of Indirect Rule
B) French to replace their policy of Assimilation
C) British on their arrival in West Africa
D)  French on their departure from West Africa.
Answer: b
Solution: The Policy of Association was adopted by France to replace its earlier policy of Assimilation.

papers.subject: Government

papers.sourceText:
Q: The last measure used by the pressure groups issuing a condition to be satisfied within a stipulated time is called_______
A) Lobbying
B) Ultimatum
C) Dialogue
D) Strike
Answer: b
Solution: Pressure groups commonly issued deadlines(ultimatum) for the government to fulfill their requests and queries before embarking on strike action.

Q: A vote of no confidence means______
A) the same as impeachment in a presidential system
B)  the ability of the head of state to dissolve the parliament when collective responsibility fails to hold
C) the act of showing disapproval to the prime minister having breached the collective responsibility doctrine
D)  the disapproval with dismissal in effect, the ministers and its head
Answer: d
Solution: A vote of no confidence is a formal motion passed by the legislature (parliament) to indicate that the government (headed by the Prime Minister) no longer has the support of the majority. When passed:

The Prime Minister and the entire cabinet must resign.
It usually leads to the formation of a new government or a call for fresh elections.

Q: The Green Revolution programme was the effected manifesto of the ........ in 1979
A) UPN
B) NPN
C) NPP
D) GNPP
Answer: b
Solution: The National Party of Nigeria (NPN) is popularly known for its Green Revolution agricultural project in the late 1979s.

Q: ____ is noted for having said "man by nature is a political animal"
A) Thomas Hobbes
B) Aristotle
C) Plato
D)  J.J Rosseau
Answer: b
Solution: According to Aristotle, every human interaction intersects with political determinations and interests.

Q: The right of a citizen to seek redress means the right to________
A) fair hearing
B) free access to legal materials
C) seek an appeal under another judgement
D) exercise his political liberty
Answer: c
Solution: Seek an appeal under another judgement is the best answer because,  ''the right to seek redress'' is a fundamental element of rule of law. It means that aggrieved parties should be afforded the opportunity to have their cases re-examined especially by a court of higher authority.

Q: The non-stratified society in the pre-colonial era was that of the ........ where decisions were made________
A) Yoruba, by the Oyomesi
B) Igbo, by consensus
C) Hausa/Fulani, by the Emir
D)  Igbo, by the Okpara
Answer: b
Solution: The Igbo precolonial was seen as ''headless'' and decisions were made based on popular consultations and acceptability.

Q: The newspaper established by Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe to project the interest of nationalists was__________
A)  West African Pilot
B) Lagos Weekly Record
C) Daily Times
D) The Comet
Answer: a
Solution: The West African Pilot was the newspaper of Dr Azikiwe which served as a medium for propagating nationalist ideas and solidarity movements towards self-realization.

Q: The federal judge under the 1963 constitution could be removed by the______
A) 2/3 majority of the National Assembly
B) Federal Judicial Service Commission
C) Nigerian Judicial Council
D) Executive president
Answer: a
Solution: 2/3 majority support or vote of the National Assembly members was enough under the 1963 Constitution to remove a federal judge.

Q: The area from which one or more members or representatives are elected in public offices is called the electoral ........
A) College
B) Constituency
C) Ward
D) District
Answer: b
Solution: Constituency is the definition for the political area from which an individual is elected into a representative office.

Q: In a democratic system _______
A) Majority Vote
B)  Legal Sovereignty shouldn't be unquestionable
C) Electoral college is always necessary
D) Minority vote but majority rule
Answer: b
Solution: Legal sovereignty shouldn't be unquestionable because in a democratic system, the powers of the legislature should be subject to necessary executive and judicial review respectively for the sake of checks and balance and accountability.

Q: Under the 1999 constitution, the Chief Law Officer and the Supreme Court Judge respectively are the_______ 
A) Chief Justice, Chief Judge
B)  Minister of Justice, Chief Judge
C) Attorney-General, Chief Justice
D) Chief Registrar of the Supreme Court, Chief Justice
Answer: c
Solution: The Attorney General of the Federation is the same as the Minister of Justice while the judge at the Supreme Court level is the Chief Justice.s

Q: Generally, a political party with only manifestoes without fulfilment is a/an _____
A)  conservative party
B)  elitist party
C) theocratic party
D) republican party
Answer: b
Solution: Elitist is often used as a critique label, to describe a political party definitive of social class and rankings of top profiled politicians without much agenda for social justice. Elitist parties are often seen as focusing more on presenting themselves as representatives of a particular elite or ideology rather than actively implementing their policies or fulfilling their promises.

Q: The political party serves as________
A)  A platform upon which the rights and liberties of the people can be attained
B) The group aggregating the interest of all in the state
C) A platform for rebelling against military rule
D) A platform for interest representation
Answer: d
Solution: A political party primarily serves as a platform for interest representation by:

Organizing and representing the views and interests of different groups in society.
Competing for political power through elections.
Influencing government policies in favor of their supporters.

Q: Lobbying is often a strategy adopted by________
A) political parties
B) public corporations
C) public authorities
D) pressure groups
Answer: d
Solution: Pressure groups often adopt lobbying as a negotiation mechanism with critical governement stakeholders and or legislators so that significant policies and laws giving effect to their interests are implemented.

Q: The Hausa/Fulani Empire as a result of its heterogeneous population adopted_________
A) A unitary system where full concentration of power prevailed
B) A federal structure where powers were decentralized although autocratic
C) A quasi federal structure with devolution
D)  A partial federal set up with deconcentration
Answer: d
Solution: The hausa/fulani empire for geo-political reasons apportioned different portfolios of authorities for serve the multiplicity of functions and administrative interests. The offices of Sarkin fada, as head of palace workers, Waziri as prime minister among others are pointers in this regard.

Q: Twelve States creation is a known achievement of the ... Regime
A) Abdulsalam Abubakar's
B) Ibrahim Babaginda's
C) Yakubu Gowon's
D) Murtala Mohammed's
Answer: c
Solution: Yakubu Gowon created 12 states for Nigeria in 1967.

Q: The Brussel conference in 1889/90 was based on______
A) putting an end to slave trade
B)  the scramble for Africa
C) furthering the decision on colonialism as previously discussed in the Berlin conference
D) deciding on how to penetrate Africa for economic adventurism
Answer: a
Solution: The Brussel Conference unlike the Berlin Conference was targeted at the reconsideration of the unjust virtues and vices occasioned by colonialism, thereby specifically seeking to eradicate slave trade and related activities.

Q: An order compelling a lower court or public corporation to perform in accordance with legitimacy is called_________
A) the writ of mandamus
B) the great writ
C) the writ of ombudsman
D) none of the above
Answer: a
Solution: Writ (i.e Order) of Mandamus is usually issued to mandate a public authority to perform its statutory or the functions tied to its establishment. On the alternative, the great writ means the habeas corpus writ issued to order the release of a body or person unlawfully detained or imprisoned to stand judgement

Q: Nigeria's federalism is often considered a flaw along the standard test of the Classical federalism ideology labelled along with_______
A) Abraham Lincoln
B) K.C Wheare
C) Thomas Hobbes
D) Aristotle
Answer: b
Solution: Kenneth Clinton Wheare is noted to having postulated that the fundamental, negotiable element of federalism is voluntary submission of rights by the component units in a federal set up.

Q: That type of sovereignty that thrives on legitimacy is__________
A)  external sovereignty
B) vested on any form of government
C) legal sovereignty
D) within the people's mandate
Answer: c
Solution: Legal sovereignty expresses his will in legal terms. This means it can only declare according to law the will of the state.

Q: Popular political participation means________
A) having majority of the people partaking in politics
B)  having a good number of voters in the electoral process
C) the aggregate efforts of more than half of the citizens to partake in public debate and politics
D) the sum total of all activities exerted by the majority with enthusiasm actively involving in all aspects of their political sphere
Answer: d
Solution: The sum total of all activities exerted by the majority with enthusiasm actively involving in all aspects of their political sphere is the best answer not only because is the all-encompassing answer but also because popular political participation is the aggregation of all efforts of the citizens partaking deliberately and consciously in their governance affairs.

Q: A form of government organized by a council of military officers is called______
A) Militocracy
B) Stratocracy
C) Military Junta
D) Mobocracy
Answer: b
Solution: A stratocracy is a form of government headed by military chiefs.

Q: Argumentation, negotiation and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begins at the_______
A) third stage
B)  first reading
C) committee stage
D)  second reading
Answer: d
Solution: The second reading is where debate, argumentation, negotiation, and deliberation on the subject matter of a bill begin. At this stage:

Lawmakers discuss the general principles of the bill.
They debate its merits and implications before deciding whether it should progress to the next stage.
If the bill passes the second reading, it moves to the committee stage for detailed examination.

Q: Deconcentration of power means the_______
A) sharing of powers among tiers of government
B) creation of semi autonomous units to govern other parts of a state
C) process of setting strategies or policies for the subsidiary territories in the state by putting recognized personnel in place
D) act of delegating powers and authority to component units that exist in a state
Answer: c
Solution: Deconcentration involves the passing down of selected administrative functions to lower levels or units within government agencies or departments with the centre remaining in control

Like the series of political office arrangements and portfolios in the Hausa/Fulani Empire i.e the Galadima, Waziri and the rest, deconcentration of power is obtainable unlike in devolution which Options B and D implicitly cover. Option A refers to the Decentralization of powers.

Q: A form of government which has its slogan to be 'ruling of the best' is__________
A) democracy
B) aristocracy
C) timocracy
D) plutocracy
Answer: b
Solution: Aristocracy being a rule by the Noble is believed to be a ruling of the best class of persons. Timocracy on the other hand, is believed by Aristotle to be a government strictly by property-owners with emphasis on honour and proprietary interest holdings.

Q: Class stratification is a peculiar feature of___________
A) capitalism
B) communism
C) socialism
D) feudalism
Answer: a
Solution: In a capitalist system, there is a clear differentiation gap between the ruling class and the ruled or the proletarates.

Q: Executive Council of the African Union makes decision by_______
A) 1/3 majority vote
B) discretion
C) consensus
D)  the veto of the General Secretariat
Answer: c
Solution: The Council of Ministers of the State Parties of the AU, the Executive Council makes decision primarily by consensus or by 2/3 majority support.

Q: The Economic and Financials Crime Commission (EFCC) scope and nature of duty may not extend to_______
A) arresting suspects of cyber crime and online fraud
B)  arresting the giver and the taker in a corruption case
C)  conducting trials and punishing persons involved in corruption matters
D) investigating cases of substance and drug abuse intersecting with money laundering
Answer: c
Solution: The EFCC as it is, is an executive body that must discharge its functions strictly in line with the reasons for its establishment. None of those functions extend to exercising judicial powers by punishing and conducting trials for suspects, which the strict duty of the court.

Q: One of the following reasons is unlikely to necessitate the emergence of a federal system?
A) social factors
B) geographical factors
C) cultural diversity
D) political sovereignty
Answer: d
Solution: Other options are necessary reasons for the adoption of a federal system except for sake of defining or strengthening the political sovereignty which invariably belongs to the citizens.

Q: The fact that the office of the Chairman is rotational in ECOWAS makes it a perfect example of a/an ........
A) Cartel
B) Confederacy
C) Economic and Egalitarian political mergers
D) Collegiate
Answer: d
Solution: A collegiate system refers to a system where leadership is shared or rotated among members rather than being permanently held by one entity.

In ECOWAS (Economic Community of West African States), the Chairmanship is rotational among member states, meaning no single country or leader permanently dominates the organization.
This makes ECOWAS a collegiate body, where power is collectively exercised and shared.

Q: The delineation of electoral constituencies for reasons of political advantage is termed___________
A) dissolution
B) prorogation
C) gerrymandering
D) delimitation
Answer: c
Solution: Gerrymandering is the process of creating political constituencies in order to favour the electoral scores of a political party.

Q: In the 4th republic, the political parties were______
A) NAP, PDP and APGA
B)  PDP, APP, AD
C) UPGA, NNA, CAN
D)  PDP, APGA, AD
Answer: d
Solution: With a multiparty system, the three political parties in 4th Republic were the Peoples Democratic Party, All Progressive Grand Alliance and the Alliance for Democracy.

Q: A party can be said to have national outlook if________
A)  it is ethnic based but has branches all over the state
B) its membership cut across ethnic boundaries
C) it is registered by the electoral commission as a national party
D) it is headed by individuals who are famous within and without the country
Answer: b
Solution: A political party has a national outlook when it represents diverse ethnic, religious, and regional groups rather than being limited to a specific ethnic or regional interest.

Q: The basis of the Nigerian foreign policy thrust particularly during the Independence Constitution era was ... in nature
A) afrocentric
B) eurocentric
C) neo-colonialistic
D) anti-apartheid
Answer: a
Solution: Afrocentrism is the term used to describe the nature and interests of the Nigerian foreign policy targets withy preference for African neighboring States.

Q: Amendment of the U. N. O. charter is the duty of the ........
A)  Security Council
B) Secretariat
C) General Assembly
D) Trusteeship Councils
Answer: c
Solution: The UN General Assembly has the duty of amending relevant provisions of the UN Charter.

Q: Implementations of the target programmes of the government is the primary duty of the _____ a part of the _____
A) Courts; Judiciary
B)  Public Service; Civil Service
C)  Civil Service; Public Service
D) Ministers; Ministry of Works
Answer: c
Solution: The Civil Service is an integral branch of the public service which primarily functions to implement the policies of the government.

Q: In most recent times, a seemingly workable solution to the Nigerian federal question is that of_______
A) state police
B) restructuring
C) terrorism
D) revenue allocation
Answer: b
Solution: Although Options A, B and C are recurring options for the Nigerian federalism, the clarion call for restructuring is louder than ever before.

Q: The most representative organ of the united nations is the_______
A)  General Assembly
B) Security Council
C) Economic and Social Council
D)  International Court of Justice
Answer: a
Solution: General Assembly. The UN General Assembly comprises the Heads of State and Government of all the State Parties in the UN body.

Q: The term ultra vires means_________
A) the exercise of supervisory functions by the judiciary
B) a situation where a public authority dutifully performs its functions
C) a situation where a public authority acts beyond the scope of its duties
D) the act of exercising administrative competence over a matter
Answer: c
Solution: A public authority is said to have ultra vires when it has acted beyond the boundaries of its duties as provided for in its enabling law or as prescribed by the Executive.

Q: According to Lewis Samuel, '________ is identified with pure conquest and unequivocal exploitation...'
A) Neo colonialism
B) Progressive Imperialism
C)  Regressive Imperialism
D)  Colonialism
Answer: c
Solution: The ideology of regressive imperialism is pure economic advantage and enrichment of the imperialists devoid of any ethical consideration.s
