Q: Subscription in advance is treated in the balance sheet as a
A)  current asset
B) current liability
C) fixed asset
D) long term liability
Answer: b
Solution: current assets are assets of the company that can be easily converted to cash when needed

current liability: this is the liability owned to outsiders but still enjoying its benefit within a year e.g creditors, wages in arrears

Q: What is the effect of transaction when cash is paid into the bank
A) Bank balance decrease and cash balance increase
B)  bank balance decrease and cash balance decrease
C) cash balance increase and bank balance increase
D) cash balance decrease and bank balance increase
Answer: d
Solution: Cash balance decrease and bank balance increase: The cash as leaving the cash till and will be deposited into the bank

Q: The following appears in trading account except
A) sales
B) carriage outward
C) carriage inward
D) opening stock
Answer: b
Solution: carriage outward: it is the cost of transporting goods from the company to the buyer. it is on debit side of the profit and loss account because it is an expenses incurred on distributing the goods to customer.

Q: A double entry for a transaction that offsets one amount against another on both sides of the cashbook is a
A) original entry
B)  contra entry
C)  prime entry
D)  contract entry
Answer: b
Solution: contra entry is used to offset amount or same transaction against another on both side of the cashbook

Q: The correct expression of accounting equation is
A)  Assets = Liabilities + Equity
B) Net assets = Liabilities + Equity
C) Assets + Liabilities = Equity
D) Assets = Equity - liabilities
Answer: a
Solution: The fundamental accounting equation is Asset = Capital + Liabilities
Asset = Liabilities + Equity the total assets of the company is generated through liabilities to outsiders that the company is still enjoying in addition with the equity by the owners of the business

Q: The account where the profit are distributed to the partner in their profit sharing ratio in partnership
A)  trading account
B) appropriation account
C) balance sheet
D) profit and loss account
Answer: b
Solution: Appropriation account is the account into which the net profit found in the profit and loss account of the partner will be carried down to and will be shared according to their sharing ratio

Q: Two departments A and B have the following information: Department A has Sales ₦250,000, Purchases ₦150,000, Discount received ₦24,000, and Discount allowed ₦15,000. Department B has Sales ₦500,000 and Purchases ₦250,000. Calculate the discount received in Department B.
A) ₦12,000
B) ₦40,000
C)  ₦16,000
D) ₦9,000
Answer: b
Solution: Department A’s discount‑received rate is ₦24 000 ÷ ₦150 000 = 16%. Applying this to Department B’s purchases (₦250 000) gives ₦250 000 × 16% = ₦40 000 as the discount received by Department B.

Q: An advantage of FIFO method of stock valuation is that
A) it serves-as a control during inflation
B) it is calculated at the end of the year
C)  it is progressive in nature
D) its flow of cost is in sequence with the flow of stock.
Answer: d
Solution: The major advantage of the first in first out(FIFO) method of stock valuation

1. it is very easy to apply

2. no manipulation of income is possible

3. the balance sheet amount for inventory is likely to approximate the current market value

4. its flow of cost is in sequence with the flow of stock. Since the first stock will be considered for sale before other stock. the cost is always in sequence with the flow of stock because it corresponds with the normal physical flow of goods

Q: You add the following when starting with the balance as per cash book when preparing the bank reconciliation statement except
A) Unpresented
B) Dividend
C) Uncredited cheque
D) credit transfer
Answer: c
Solution: Uncredited cheque: This have to be deducted when starting balance as per cash book

Q: What is the main purpose of transaction file?
A) To record assets and liabilities
B) To update income and expenses
C) to update master files
D)  to make organization decision
Answer: c
Solution: The main purpose of organization file is to update the master file of the organization

Q: When starting with the cash book balance in preparing the bank reconciliation statement, the followings are added
A) Unpresented cheque
B) Dividend
C)  Uncredited cheque
D) credit transfer
Answer: c
Solution: Uncredited cheque have to be less when starting with balance as per cashbook not add because the cheque are yet to be credited by the bank

Q: Which of these is the main source document for recording cash paid into bank?
A) invoice
B) cheque book
C) credit note
D) pay-in-slip
Answer: d
Solution: Pay-in-slip:this is in form of a slip designed with the name of the bank on top that has dates amounts in figure and word, column for the denomination of money paid in signature bank teller, stamp to prove the money is deposited into the bank

Q: A business has the following bank reconciliation information: Balance as per cashbook ₦5,467, Uncredited cheques ₦4,410, Unpresented cheques ₦19,404, and Cheques wrongly debited by bank ₦1,404. What is the balance as per bank statement?
A)  ₦21,901
B) ₦19,057
C)  ₦21,109
D)  ₦21,091
Answer: b
Solution: Starting from the cashbook balance of ₦5,467, we adjust for items not yet reflected in the bank statement:

Add unpresented cheques (outstanding at bank): ₦19,404

Subtract uncredited cheques (lodgements in transit): ₦4,410

Subtract cheques wrongly debited by the bank (the bank has already taken this amount): ₦1,404

So the bank statement balance is:
5,467 + 19,404 − 4,410 − 1,404 = ₦19,057

Q: The tier of government that uses financial memorandum
A) Federal government
B)  state government
C)  local government
D) municipal government
Answer: c
Solution: In Nigeria, the Financial Memorandum is the guiding document issued by the State Accountant‑General that lays down the detailed rules and procedures for budget preparation, expenditure control, accounting, and reporting at the local government level. None of the other tiers use a standalone “financial memorandum” in the same way.

Q: One of the options below have the same features as the profit and loss account in non-profit organization
A) Income and expenditure account
B)  profit and loss account
C) receipts and payment account
D) Non profit account
Answer: a
Solution: Income and expenditure : This is the type of account that operate same features as the profit and loss account it takes in consideration all arrears and prepayments

Q: A business has the following information for a trading period: Stock Jan 1 ₦2600, Purchases ₦4000, Carriage inwards ₦500, Sales ₦9000, Carriage outwards ₦500. Determine the net profit.
A)  ₦4,000
B) ₦4,500
C) . ₦5,000
D) ₦1,400
Answer: d
Solution: Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases + Carriage inwards
= ₦2,600 + ₦4,000 + ₦500
= ₦7,100

Gross profit = Sales − Cost of goods sold
= ₦9,000 − ₦7,100
= ₦1,900

Net profit = Gross profit − Carriage outwards
= ₦1,900 − ₦500
= ₦1,400.

Q: Salaries in arrears is treated in the balance sheet as a
A)  current asset
B) current liability
C) fixed asset
D) long term liability
Answer: b
Solution: Current Liability: salaries in arrears fall into the category of them under the current liability because it is benefit due to outsiders but still enjoying by the organisation and can't exceed a year

Q: The principle of double entry developed from the axioms of accounting equation is given as
A)  Assets + Liability = Equity
B) Assets + Equity = Liabilities
C) Liabilities + Equity = Asset
D) Liabilities + Equity = Net assets
Answer: c
Solution: Liabilities + Equity = Asset is given as the fundamental equation

Q: The accounting entries for goods stolen in branch will be to debit
A)  The accounting entries for goods stolen in branch will be to debit
B)  branch stock account and credit branch adjustment account
C) branch adjustment account and credit profit and loss account
D) branch adjustment account and credit branch stock account
Answer: a
Solution: A branch account is a small part of business account operating with some degree of independence . It maintains its own personal/self accounting entries to determine the profit/loss made by a specific period of time

The accounting entries is to debit profit and loss account and credit branch stock. The profit and loss is debited because the cost of the stolen goods must be charged against the profit for the period to balance the account and the branch stock account is credited because the cost of the goods is out of the branch already.

Q: In the period of rising prices, which method of stock valuation is most appropriate?
A) Last in First Out
B)  weighted average
C)  First in First Out
D) Simple average
Answer: a
Solution: Last in first out:when price rise it results to lower bet income because the leftover inventory might be extremely old and perhaps obsolete

Q: When expenses are paid on behalf of the venture, the accounting entries is to debit
A) bank account and credit joint venture account
B) expenses account and credit bank account
C)  joint venture account and credit expenses account
D) joint venture account and credit bank account
Answer: d
Solution: Joint venture account is an account that all expenditure incurred for the venture is debited and all income is credited to.
Debit joint venture and credit bank account because expenses incurred on behalf of the venture has to be debited to the joint venture account and since the money is joint out the bank must be credited to balance the account

Q: The following are the importance of branch account except
A) it enable the organization to determine the branch that is making either profit or loss
B)  it allows proper control over the branch by the head office
C) it assist the organization to determine the performance of a branch manager
D) it allows fraud and wastage of resources
Answer: d
Solution: The activities and resources of branches is strictly monitored by the head office and each branch is supplied according to its need so it will be difficult to commit fraud or waste any resources

Q: Given:
I. Settlement of debts
II. Cessation of business
III. Introduction of assets
IV. Disposal of assets
Which of these constitutes dissolution of partnership?
A) II and IV only
B)  I, II and IV only
C)  I, II and III only
D)  II, III and IV only
Answer: b
Solution: Dissolution of partnership business simply means the break up of partnership business and which are caused by many factors
II,III and IV: disposal of asset does not constitute dissolution

Q: Discount allowed is enjoyed by
A) Managers
B) Customers
C) Suppliers
D) Staff of the company
Answer: b
Solution: Customer: customers are the one that enjoys discount allowed. It is allowed to them by the suppliers. it can be in cash or trade

Q: Which of these is the subsidiary book for return inwards?
A) Sales day book
B) Sales return journal
C)  Purchases day journal
D) Cash book
Answer: b
Solution: Sales return journal otherwise called return inward book is meant for recording of all good returned by customer

Q: An evidence of payment issued to a government ministry by a revenue collector is
A) treasury receipt
B)  receipt voucher
C) payment voucher
D)  treasury card
Answer: b
Solution: Receipt voucher is raised as evidence by revenue collector when government funds and property or received

Receipt voucher: these are vouchers raised as evidence for the receipt of government funds and property. The revenue collected is prepared for the government ministry as a means that revenue has been collected

Q: In manufacturing account, depreciation of office machine is charged to
A) trading account
B) appropriation account
C) balance street
D) profit and loss account
Answer: d
Solution: profit and loss account: the depreciation of the office machine is considered as part of administrative expense which must be charged against the profit of the company

Q: The discount column on the left-hand side of cashbook represents a discount
A) received from a creditor
B) allowed to a debtor
C) received from a debtor
D) allowed to a creditor
Answer: b
Solution: Allowed to a debtor: the debit side of the cashbook is where all proceeds from sales are recorded and have to be matched with the discount allowed to the debtor /creditor

Q: Given:
I. It records subscription in arrears
II. Payments of liabilities is effected
III. The account does not show if cash payment is revenue or capital expenditure
IV. It performs the same function as cashbook
The features of receipts and payment account includes
A) I, II and IV

B) II,III and IV

C) III and IV

D) I, II and III
Answer: b
Solution: A Receipts and Payments Account:

II. Records the payment of liabilities as they’re settled in cash.

III. Does not distinguish whether cash payments are for revenue or capital items.

IV. Functions in the same way as a cashbook, summarizing all cash and bank receipts and payments.

It does not record transactions on an accrual basis (so it does not capture subscriptions in arrears), making statement I incorrect.

Q: Which of these is a content of a master file?
A) All records relevant to the organisation.
B) Records of assets of the organisation
C) A collection of data items
D)  All records relating to employees
Answer: a
Solution: All record relevant to the organization: the records which are only relevant to the organization such as the name and address as well as summary information such as amount due and year to date sales will be in master file

Q: Two departments A and B have the following information: Department A has Sales ₦250,000, Purchases ₦500,000, Discount received ₦24,000, and Discount allowed ₦15,000. Department B has Sales ₦150,000 and Purchases ₦250,000. Determine the discount allowed by Department A.
A)  ₦5,000
B) ₦9,375
C) ₦5,625
D) ₦8,000
Answer: b
Solution: Step 1: Calculate total sales

Department A sales: ₦250,000
Department B sales: ₦150,000
Total sales: ₦400,000

Step 2: Calculate Department A's proportion of total sales
Department A's proportion = ₦250,000 ÷ ₦400,000 = 62.5%
Step 3: Allocate total discount allowed proportionally
Total discount allowed = ₦15,000 (given for the business)
Department A's discount allowed = ₦15,000 × 62.5% = ₦9,375
Department A's discount allowed is ₦9,375, representing their proportional share based on sales volume.

Q: The use of a three column cash book is determined by
A) cash discount
B) trade discount
C) cash transaction
D) Bank transaction
Answer: a
Solution: A cash discount is a deduction allowed by the seller of goods or by the provider of services in order to motivate the customer to pay within a specified time

Q: Goodwill can be created in the books of a partnership firm when
A) the partnership experiences super profit
B)  a new member is admitted
C) the business is being expanded
D)  the business suffers high loss
Answer: a
Solution: The partnership experiences super profit: super profit is the profit that is generated by intangible asset or the profit that is attributed by the tangible asset when such profit is capitalized we get intangible asset or goodwill

Q: A business acquisition shows the following assets and liabilities: Plant and Machinery ₦190,000, Motor Vehicle ₦170,000, Stock ₦60,000, Current Liabilities ₦50,000, Purchase consideration ₦400,000. Determine the amount of goodwill.
A) ₦110 000
B)  ₦80 000
C)  ₦90 000
D)  ₦30 000
Answer: d
Solution: Net assets acquired = (₦190,000 + ₦170,000 + ₦60,000) – ₦50,000 = ₦420,000 – ₦50,000 = ₦370,000
Goodwill = Purchase consideration – Net assets = ₦400,000 – ₦370,000 = ₦30,000.

Q: A company's inventory records show the following information for the year: Opening stock on January 1st was ₦2,000, purchases during the year totaled ₦4,000, carriage inwards was ₦500, sales amounted to ₦9,000, and carriage outwards was ₦500. Based on this information, what is the value of the Gross profit?
A) ₦9,000
B)  ₦2,500
C) ₦3,000
D) ₦1,500
Answer: b
Solution: 
COGS = 2,000 + 4,000 + 500 = ₦6,500

Gross Profit = Sales − COGS = 9,000 − 6,500 = ₦2,500

Q: Which of these accounts is dissolution expenses credited?
A) partners capital account
B) revaluation account
C) partners current account
D) Realization account
Answer: d
Solution: Realization account: the cash realized from sales of asset is credited to it

Q: one of the options below is not the source of income for non- profit organization
A) Entrance fees
B) subscription/dues
C) odrinary shares
D) Donations
Answer: c
Solution: Ordinary shares: This type of source of income is only used in profit oriented organization to generate fund the pubic so as to enable the organization make more profit at the end of a specified period

Q: The current growth in the volume of trading and financial dealing in Nigeria is helped by
A) increased financial activities
B) government intervention
C)  credit as a factor in business
D) Payment for goods in cashc
Answer: c
Solution: The availability of credit allows businesses and consumers to purchase goods and services beyond their immediate cash resources, thereby increasing the volume of transactions and financial dealings. While cash payments, government intervention, and broader financial activities all play roles in the economy, it is the extension of credit that most directly fuels higher trading volumes by enabling deferred payments and greater purchasing power.

Q: Which type of cashbook entry involves recording the same amount on both the debit and credit sides to offset each other?
A) Contra entry
B) Compound entry
C) Transfer entry
D) Journal entry
Answer: a
Solution: A contra entry in the cashbook is used when the business moves money between its own cash and bank accounts—such as depositing cash into the bank or withdrawing cash from the bank

Q: Given:
I. Cash refunds
II. Debit note issued
III. Dishonored cheque
IV. Purchases
The item on the credit side of purchases ledger control account includes
A)  I, II and III only
B)  I and II only
C) III and IV only
D) I, III and IV only
Answer: c
Solution: The credit side of the Purchases Ledger Control Account shows items that increase the amount you owe to suppliers. These are:

III. Dishonoured cheque, because a bounced cheque reverses a payment and increases your outstanding balance.

IV. Purchases, as credit purchases directly raise your payables.

Cash refunds (I) and debit notes issued (II) reduce what you owe and therefore appear on the debit side.

papers.sourceText: Q: The factor that determine the periodic depreciation charge are? A) asset cost, market value and useful life B) asset cost, market value and residusl value C) asset value, cash value useful life D) asset cost, salvage and useful life Answer: d Solution: To calculate periodic depreciation, you need three key factors: 1. Asset Cost (Original Cost) The initial purchase price of the asset What you paid to acquire the asset 2. Salvage Value (Residual Value) The estimated value of the asset at the end of its useful life What you expect to get when you dispose of the asset 3. Useful Life The estimated period the asset will be used in the business How long the asset will generate economic benefits Depreciation Formula: Annual Depreciation = (Asset Cost - Salvage Value) ÷ Useful Life Q: Opening balance of Diksacompany was 12, 202, closing balance N15,300, total cash received during the period N40, 000. What was the amount of cash paid during the same period? A) N36. 902 B) N27,502 C) N12,498 D) N43.098 Answer: c Q: (i) Fixtures account (ii) Machinery account (iii) Wages accounts (iv) Rent account. Which of the above are nominal account? A) iii and iv B) i and ii C) i and iii D) ii and iii Answer: a Solution: Wages and rent are nominal (expense) accounts. Fixtures and machinery are real (asset) accounts. Q: Which of the following is a debit item in the sales ledger control account A) Cheque reciepts B) Dishonoured cheques C) Discount allowed D) Bills recievable Answer: b Solution: The Sales Ledger Control Account is a summary account that records transactions with debtors (customers). Dishonoured cheques increase the amount owed by a debtor (because the payment failed), so it is a debit item. Cheque receipts, discount allowed, and bills receivable all reduce what debtors owe, so they are credit items. Q: The income and expenditure account of a club is the same as A) single entry account B) a profit and loss account C) a trading account D) a cash book Answer: b Solution: The income and expenditure account of a club serves exactly the same purpose as a profit and loss account in a trading concern: it summarizes all the revenues (incomes) and the expenses (expenditures) for the period to show the net surplus or deficit. Q: A pension granted to any past president or vice-president shall be charged to the A) consolidated revenue fund B) special pension fund C) contingency fund D) development fund. Answer: b Q: Goods were purchased for resale on credit costing ₦150,000 on 30th September 2008 from Tosanwumi International. The entry to record these transaction is debit A) Tosanwumi International, credit purchase Account B) Purchase Account ₦150,000, credit Tosanwumi International Account ₦150,000 C) Credit Account ₦150,000, Credit Tosanwumi International ₦150,000 D) Tosanwumi International ₦150,000, credit credit Account ₦150,000 Answer: b Solution: When a purchase was made, a credit purchase invoice would have been issued by the supplier, Tosanwumi International, which would be signed by Mr. Roi as evidence of his acceptance of liability to pay for the goods. The two accounts needed to record this transaction are the purchase Account and Tosanwumi International Account. purchase account would be debited while the Tosanwumi International Account credited. Q: The expenses incurred in promoting a company are A) promoters’ expenses B) floating expenses C) preliminary expenses D) the Board’s expenses Answer: c Q: The double entry to record the goodwill in the books is debit A) Cash Account and credit Goodwill Account B) Goodwill Account and credit Purchase of Business Account C) Goodwill Account and credit Cash Account D) Purchase of Business Account and credit Cash Account Answer: b Q: In the absence of a sales day book or sales account the credit for sales can be computed from A) creditors control account B) debtors control account C) opening figures of the balance sheet D) closing figures of the balance sheet Answer: b Solution: The debtors control account (sales ledger control account) summarizes all transactions with customers. In the absence of a sales day book, you can compute total credit sales by analyzing this account because it records credit sales, receipts, returns, and discounts related to debtors. Q: The balance on the provision for depreciation account is? A) added to fixed assets on the balance sheet B) deducted from the fixed assets on the balance sheet C) deducted from the profitand loss account D) added to current liabilities of the account Answer: b Solution: Reason: Provision for depreciation (accumulated depreciation) is a contra-asset account, it reduces the gross carrying amount of fixed assets to show their net book value on the balance sheet. Q: Use the information below to answer questions 17 and 18 If at 31/1/95 the following information was ascertained (i)Rent shop ₦12,000 paid for the year (ii) Total purchases ₦15,000 (iii) Total sales ₦8,200 (iv) Stock of goods left ₦10,000 (v) Paid sales boy ₦500. What is the balance on its cash account as at 31/1/95? A) ₦22,800 B) ₦21,200 C) ₦9,200 D) ₦800 Answer: c Solution: Starting with the opening cash-in-hand of ₦28 500 and then accounting for the month’s cash movements: Add: Cash receipts from sales ₦ 8 200 Less: Purchases paid ₦15 000 Less: Rent paid ₦12 000 Less: Sales–boy salary paid ₦ 500 Closing cash balance = 28,500 + 8,200 − 15,000 − 12,000 − 500 = ₦9200 Q: Excess of current assets over current liabilities is A) deferred capital. B) nominal capital. C) working capital D) authorized capital. Answer: c Q: If creditors at 1/1/10 were Le 3,000; creditors at 31/12/10 Le 5,500 and payments to creditors Le 29,000. The purchases figure for 2010 is A) Le 34,500 B) Le 32,000 C) Le 31,500 D) Le 26,500 Answer: c Q: Bala Ltd acquired the business of Bello Ltd and caused the separate existence of the latter company to terminate. This situation is best described as? A) absorption B) merger C) conversion D) dissolution Answer: a Solution: This situation is best described as absorption. Absorption occurs when: One existing company (Bala Ltd) takes over another existing company (Bello Ltd) The acquired company (Bello Ltd) loses its separate legal identity and ceases to exist The acquiring company (Bala Ltd) continues to exist and absorbs all assets and liabilities Only one company survives the transaction Q: If a sole proprietorship is purchased for cash, then? A) the purchaser debits his business purchase account with the consideration he pays B) all assets and liabilities must be bought C) goodwill results where value of assets D) the vendor debits his business purchase account with the considerstion he receives Answer: a Solution: The purchaser records the total purchase price in a "Business Purchase Account" or similar account, which is then analyzed and allocated to individual assets and goodwill. Q: The return on debenture holding is A) share bonus B) interest C) net profit D) dividend Answer: b Solution: Debentures are essentially loans that a company issues to investors. In return for investing in the debenture, the investor receives periodic interest payments at a predetermined rate. This interest is a fixed obligation of the company, regardless of its profitability. Q: Gross profit in the branch adjustment account is transferred to the branch? A) trading account B) receipts and payments account C) profit and loss account D) income and expenditure account Answer: a Solution: The gross profit from the branch adjustment account is transferred to the trading account, where it combines with head office gross profit to show the total gross profit of the business. Q: five hundred naria monthly is allowed on an imprest system. The following transactions took place. Period1: Cash advanced to petty cashier......₦500 Petty cashier paid out: stamp.......₦200 ₦ewspaper...........................₦250 Period 2: Cash to petty cashier...............₦450 Cashier paid for writing materials..₦350 What was the balance of cash with the petty cashier at the end of period 1? A) ₦50 B) ₦200 C) ₦300 D) ₦450 Answer: a Solution: From Period 1: Cash given = ₦500 Payments = ₦200 (stamp) + ₦250 (newspaper) = ₦450 Remaining cash = ₦500 − ₦450 = ₦50 Q: If rent account is debited instead of rate account, the error committed is that of; A) omission B) commission C) principle D) original entry Answer: a Solution: error of omission: An error that occurs when action has not been taken or when something has been left out. Q: Which of the following relates to cash basis of accounting? A) Accruals and prepayments are considered B) Debtors and creditors are recorded C) Fixed assets are written off in the year of purchase D) Profits are maximized Answer: d Q: A business has the following information for a trading period: Stock Jan 1 ₦2600, Purchases ₦4000, Carriage inwards ₦500, Sales ₦9000, Carriage outwards ₦500. Determine the net profit. A) ₦4,000 B) ₦4,500 C) . ₦5,000 D) ₦1,400 Answer: d Solution: Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases + Carriage inwards = ₦2,600 + ₦4,000 + ₦500 = ₦7,100 Gross profit = Sales − Cost of goods sold = ₦9,000 − ₦7,100 = ₦1,900 Net profit = Gross profit − Carriage outwards = ₦1,900 − ₦500 = ₦1,400. Q: In a three-column cash book, the discount allowed is shown on the? A) debit side B) credit side C) folio column D) memorandum column Answer: a Solution: Discount allowed is an expense (a reduction in cash received), so it’s recorded on the debit side of the three-column cash book. (By contrast, discount received is shown on the credit side.) Q: Lawal and co makes blocks and sell to builders. In computing prime cost, which of the following costs would be considered appropriate? A) Cement, sand and carriage outwards B) Water carriage inwards and cement C) Sales boys'wages, cement and sand D) Carriage outwards,carriage inwards and cement Answer: b Solution: The prime cost refers to all direct costs involved in the production of goods. This includes: Direct materials (e.g., cement, sand, water) Direct labor (e.g., workers making the blocks) Direct expenses (e.g., carriage inwards, which brings materials to the factory) Q: The accounting convention which states that the performance of a business should be determined by matching all expenses against all revenues is A) accruals B) materiality C) objectivity D) periodicity Answer: a Q: Sales ledger control account contains the total amount in respect of A) investors B) creditors C) shareholders D) debtors Answer: d Solution: The sales ledger control account (also known as the debtors control account) contains the total amount owed by all debtors - customers who have purchased goods or services on credit but have not yet paid. Q: Which of the following is a written acknowledgement of a loan to a company? A) debt B) retained profit C) reserve D) debenture Answer: d Solution: A debenture is a formal, written acknowledgment of a company’s debt—essentially a loan certificate. Q: To record the transfer of stock from one department to another, the correct entry would be to debit? A) goods outwards and credit goods inwards B) merchandise account and credit department stock account C) department transfering and credit department receivving D) department receiving and credit department transfering Answer: d Solution: You would debit the department receiving the stock and credit the department transferring the stock. Q: Given: Capital ...........₦1000 Liabilities........₦500 Assets.............₦1500 The accounting equation can be expressed as? A) ₦1000 + ₦500 + ₦1500 = ₦3000 B) ₦1000 - ₦500 + ₦1500 = ₦2000 C) ₦1000 + ₦500 = ₦1500 D) ₦1500 + ₦500 = ₦2000 Answer: c Solution: The basic accounting equation is: Assets = Capital + Liabilities Here: Assets = ₦1500 Capital = ₦1000 Liabilities = ₦500 So: ₦1000 + ₦500 = ₦1500 Q: A business has the following information for a particular period: Creditors had an opening balance of ₦3,000 and a closing balance of ₦4,000. Debtors had a closing balance of ₦6,000 but the opening balance is not given. During the period, cash received from debtors was ₦35,000, cash paid to suppliers was ₦25,000, discount allowed to customers was ₦4,000, and discount received from suppliers was ₦4,200. What is the total purchase for the period? A) ₦30,200 B) ₦30,000 C) ₦25,000 D) ₦31,200 Answer: a Solution: To find total purchases, we work with the creditors account movement: Creditors Account Analysis: Opening balance: ₦3,000 Closing balance: ₦4,000 Cash paid to suppliers: ₦25,000 Discount received from suppliers: ₦4,200 Using the creditors account formula: Opening Balance + Purchases - Cash Paid - Discount Received = Closing Balance Substituting the values: 3,000 + Purchases - 25,000 - 4,200 = 4,000 3,000 + Purchases - 29,200 = 4,000 Purchases = 4,000 + 29,200 - 3,000 Purchases = 30,200 Q: The amount paid by the buyer of a business which is sold as going concern is A) purchase consideration B) conversion fees C) consolidation fees D) premium fees Answer: a Solution: Purchase consideration is the amount that's received by the vendor company (Seller) for the assets and liabilities takeover by the purchasing company in exchange for cash or in other forms, such as issuing shares or other securities. Q: Adex Ltd. issues stock to its retail branches at cost price. The following information relates to Ede branch: Stock at branch 1st January at cost ₦400, Goods sent to branch at cost ₦8000, Returns to head office ₦340, Cash sales ₦9160, Stock at branch 31st December at cost ₦720. Calculate the cost of goods credited to the head office trading account. A) ₦7340 B) ₦7460 C) ₦7500 D) ₦7660 Answer: a Solution: The cost of goods credited to the Head Office Trading Account is computed as: Opening stock (₦400) Goods sent to branch (₦8,000) – Returns to Head Office (₦340) – Closing stock (₦720) = ₦7,340 Q: From Zahki Plc's balance sheet as at 31st December 1997, the company has the following financial position: On the equity and liabilities side - Paid up capital of ₦200,000, Share premium of ₦15,000, Profit and loss account balance of ₦60,000, Long-term loan of ₦180,000, Creditors of ₦200,000, and Other current liabilities of ₦100,000, totaling ₦755,000. On the assets side - Fixed assets of ₦300,000, Investment of ₦180,000, Stock of ₦28,000, Debtors of ₦90,000 with a provision of ₦3,000 making net debtors ₦87,000, Cash of ₦60,000, and Bank of ₦100,000, also totaling ₦755,000. What is the quick ratio? A) 0.82 : 1 B) 1:53:01 C) 0.95:1 D) 0.91:1 Answer: a Solution: Quick Ratio (Acid‐Test Ratio) is calculated as: (Current Assets − Stock)/Current Liabilities ​ Current Assets (excluding stock): Net Debtors ₦87,000 + Cash ₦60,000 + Bank ₦100,000 = ₦247,000 Current Liabilities: Creditors ₦200,000 + Other Current Liabilities ₦100,000 = ₦300,000 Quick Ratio: 247,000/300,000 ≈ 0.82:1 So the quick ratio is 0.82 : 1. Q: Purchases can be ascertained through the preparation of a A) stock account B) sales account C) total debtors’ control account D) total creditors, control account Answer: d Q: If goods purchased on account is returned, the buyer may inform the seller of the details by issuing: A) An invoice B) A debt memorandum C) A credit memorandum D) A bill Answer: c Q: Which accounting concept supports the assertion that economic reality takes precedence over legal issues? A) Realization concept B) Substance over form C) Conservatism D) Measurement concept Answer: b Solution: Reason: this concept requires transactions to be recorded according to their economic substance rather than their legal form, so economic reality takes precedence over legal form. Q: Which of the following accounts has a credit balance? A) Capital B) Cash C) Drawings D) Premises Answer: a Q: The total amount of money received on application was A) N 5600,00 B) N 220,000 C) N 800, 000 D) N 1 000 000 Answer: a Q: Goodwill can be introduced when A) the business suffers high loss B) the business is being expanded C) the partnership experience super profit D) a new member is admitted Answer: d Solution: The circumstances giving rise to the ascertainment of goodwill are: - admission of a new partner - change in profit sharing ratio - death or retirement of a partner - the business has been purchased - dissolution of a business Q: The debenture issued at price above the nominal value is Said to be issued at a A) margin B) premium C) cost price D) mark-up Answer: b Solution: When a debenture is issued at a price above its nominal (face) value, it is said to be issued at a premium. For example, if a debenture with a nominal value of ₦100 is issued for ₦110, it is issued at a premium of ₦10.

Q: Which of the following is not an inventory costing method?
A) FIFO
B) LIFO
C) Average cost method
D) LILA
Answer: d
Solution: FIFO (First-In, First-Out), LIFO (Last-In, First-Out), and the Average Cost Method are all standard inventory valuation methods.

LILA is not a recognized inventory costing method.

Q: In the head office ledger, the value of goods sent to the branch are____________
A) Debited to the branch current account
B) Debited to the head office current account
C) Credited to the head office current account
D) Credited to the branch current account
Answer: b
Solution: Branch current account is maintained in the head office books to record all transactions between the head office and the branch. This account is debited with the following:

  i. Goods sent to branch

  ii. Expenses of the branch paid by the head office

  iii. Profit of the branch

Q: If the purchase price exceeds the net assets of a company, the excess amount is debited to________________

A) Cash account
B)  purchase account
C) goodwill account
D) sales account
Answer: c
Solution: Goodwill is the excess of purchase consideration over the total value of the business

Q: Which of the following methods of invoicing goods to branches facilitate easy checks on the activities of branches?
A) Selling price
B) Fixed percentage on cost
C) Cost price
D) Invoice price
Answer: c
Solution: Goods are transferred from head office to branch at cost price, selling price and cost price plus mark up

Q: Using the following information, calculate the balance that should appear on the bank statement. The cashbook shows a balance of ₦13,560. There are unpresented cheques totaling ₦5,120, and a cheque for ₦2,300 has been paid into the bank but not yet credited. The bank has also received a dividend of ₦2,000, charged ₦280 in bank fees, and processed a standing order of ₦600.
A) ₦10,740
B) ₦11,860
C)  ₦16,380
D) ₦17,500
Answer: d
Solution: Balance per bank statement = ₦13,560 + ₦5,120 + ₦2,000 – ₦2,300 – ₦280 – ₦600 = ₦17,500.

Q: A Trading account for the year ended 31st December 2009 shows the following information:
Opening Stock: ₦32,000
Purchases: ₦40,000
Carriage inwards: ₦1,000
Less Returns: ₦2,000
Sales: ₦48,000
Less Returns: ₦2,000
Closing Stock: ₦9,000
Calculate:

What is the cost of goods available for sale?

A)  ₦20,500
B) ₦71,000
C)  ₦28,000
D) ₦27,000
Answer: b
Solution: Calculate Cost of Goods Available
Cost of Goods Available = Opening Stock + Net Purchases + Carriage Inwards
= ₦32,000 + ₦39,000 + ₦1,000 = ₦71,000

Q: To account for expenses paid by head office on behalf of the branch, the branch should___________
A) Debit profit and loss account and credit head office account
B) Debit head office account and credit cash
C) Credit cash and debit profit and loss account
D)  Credit profit and loss account and debit head office account
Answer: a
Solution: The head office maintains a book, (branch account) more or less like other personal accounts, so that any expenses incurred on behalf of the branch will also be debited to the branch account. Similarly, in the branch books, there will be head office accounts

Q: Gross profit in the branch adjustment account is transferred to the branch____________
A) Income and expenditure account
B) profit and loss account
C) receipt and payment account
D) trading account
Answer: d
Solution: In branch accounting, the Branch Adjustment Account is used to record inter‐branch adjustments such as stock transfers and branch expenses. Any gross profit worked out in this account is then transferred to the Branch Trading Account, where it becomes part of the overall trading results for that branch.

Q: In reconciling the branch and head office accounts, remittance in transit in the branch books is treated as a_____________
A) Debit entry
B)  Contra entry
C) . Credit entry
D) Reversal entry
Answer: a
Solution: In the branch’s own books, when cash is sent to head office but not yet received there, it isn’t left in the cash balance, instead the branch debits a “Remittance in Transit” asset account and credits cash. Thus, on reconciliation, the branch treats remittances in transit as debit entries.

Q: A partnership’s internal regulation are set out by________
A)  A constitution
B) A law
C) A deed
D) . An article
Answer: c
Solution: A partnership deed is a written agreement among the partners specifying rules and regulations and is signed by all the partners and stamped as per stamp act with an aim to prevent possible disputes and disagreements among the partners at future dates

Q: Use the information to answer the questions

  Rakiya and joy are in a partnership and agreed that 5% interest per annum is to be charged on drawings. The drawing made by both partners in one year were:

  Rakiya, ₦200 on March 31 and ₦300 on September 30.

  Joy, ₦100 on April 1 and ₦240 on July 1.

  The interest on Joy’s drawing is___________
A) ₦11.25
B) ₦500.00
C) ₦9.75.
D) ₦340.00
Answer: c
Solution: The interest on Joy’s drawings is ₦9.75, calculated as follows:

₦100 drawn on April 1 for 9 months:
₦100 × 5% × 9/12 = ₦3.75

₦240 drawn on July 1 for 6 months:
₦240 × 5% × 6/12 = ₦6.00

Total interest = ₦3.75 + ₦6.00 = ₦9.75.

Q: What act generally includes completing unfinished partnership business, collecting and paying debts, collecting partnership assets to be turned into cash and taking inventory?
A) Formation
B) dissolution
C)  winding up
D)  termination
Answer: b
Solution: It is the first step in termination process

Q: Why should a new partner contribute towards goodwill on his admission?
A) It is a norm
B) to ensure new partner also have a stake in the business
C) the firm into which he is entering already has some goodwill in the market
D) to purchase the business
Answer: c
Solution: Goodwill is being paid by a new partner because the partnership he is entering into already has goodwill in the market as well as to pay for the portion sacrificed by existing partners in form to their profit to admit the new partner.

Q: The amount called in respect of a share but not paid before or on the date fixed for payment is referred to as:
A) Call in advance
B) call in arrears
C) forfeiture
D) shares
Answer: b
Solution: the amount called by the company which is not paid by the shareholders before the due date fixed for payment

 

Q: Using the following:

Balance as par overdraft of the cashbook is ₦4000 ,uncredited cheque is ₦2300, bank charges ₦300, unpresented cheque ₦5000.

  what is the adjusted cashbook balance?
A) ₦4000
B) 3₦00
C) ₦4300
D) ₦5000
Answer: c
Solution: Adjusted cashbook balance=–₦4000–₦300=–₦4300

Q: In departmental accounting, which is not a transfer pricing_________
A) cost based transfer price
B) market based transfer pricing
C) Dual pricing system
D) peak pricing
Answer: d
Solution: The standard transfer‐pricing methods used in departmental accounting are:

Cost‐based transfer pricing (using internal cost as the basis)

Market‐based transfer pricing (using external market prices)

Dual pricing system (charging one price to the selling division and another to the buying division)

Peak pricing, on the other hand, is a demand‐management strategy for external customers (adjusting prices during high‐demand “peak” periods) and is not used for inter‐departmental transfer pricin

Q: Profit or loss in a partnership is usually arrived at after deducting from gross profit all expenses including____________
A)  Partners salaries
B) Interest on capital
C)  Interest on loans
D) Partners drawings
Answer: c
Solution: is charged in the profit and loss account as finance expenses

Q: A partnership deed is used to____________
A) Promote mutual understanding
B) Enhance mistrust
C) Encourage discrepancy
D) Control funds
Answer: a
Solution: Partnership deed can be used to:

  i. Indicates terms on which the business corporation us founded

  ii. To form a partnership for the purpose of doing business together

  iii. Prevent future disputes

  iv. Promote mutual understanding

  v. Avoid mistrust

Q: Transfers from the head office to branches are best carried out at__________
A) Cost price
B) Cost plus mark up
C) Selling price
D) Market price
Answer: b
Solution: Goods are transferred from head office to branch at cost price, selling price and cost price plus mark up

Q: Advertising expenses incurred on a product in a business organization should be charged to
A) Sales department
B) Production department
C)  Purchase department
D) Administration department
Answer: a
Solution: Advertising expenses are expenses incurred in order to enhance the sales of the company’s product/services

Q: Tea and Cup are into a partnership business. Interests on drawings made by partners are at 10% per annum. Tea’s capital is ₦70000 and current balance is ₦50000. He withdrew the following amounts during the year : 3000 on 31st January ,2000 on 31st March, 4000 on 1st July, 1500 on the 30th September, 2500 on 1st November. Cup’s capital is ₦100000 and current balance is ₦40000. He made no drawings during the period. What is the interest on the drawings of Tea?
A)  ₦705
B) ₦500
C) ₦1000
D) ₦10000
Answer: a
Solution: Interest on Tea’s drawings is calculated as the sum of each drawing × 10% × (months outstanding ÷ 12):

₦3 000 on 31 Jan: 3 000 × 10% × (11/12) = ₦275.00

₦2 000 on 31 Mar: 2 000 × 10% × (9/12) = ₦150.00

₦4 000 on 1 Jul: 4 000 × 10% × (6/12) = ₦200.00

₦1 500 on 30 Sep: 1 500 × 10% × (3/12) = ₦37.50

₦2 500 on 1 Nov: 2 500 × 10% × (2/12) = ₦41.67

Total interest = ₦275 + ₦150 + ₦200 + ₦37.50 + ₦41.67 = ₦704.17  ≈ ₦705..

Q: Which of the following is a common cause of a discrepancy between head office and branch trial office________
A) Stock and repayment
B) Creditors and cash in trans
C) Stock and cash in transit
D) Debtors and cash in transit
Answer: c
Solution: Goods in transit are goods sent by the head office to branch but by the close of financial year, these goods have not yet reached the branch.

 Cash in transit are cash remitted by the branch to head office by the end of the financial year this cash has not yet reached the head office

Another major cause of discrepancy is returns in transit. This is the returns by the branch to head office but by the end of the year, they have not been received by the head office

Q: During the period, Department P opened with stock of ₦2 000, made purchases of ₦2 500 and recorded sales of ₦6 000. Its closing stock was ₦1 500. Department P also received goods costing ₦300 transferred in from Department Q and incurred operating expenses of ₦200. What was Department P’s net profit for the period?
A)  ₦2,500
B) ₦2,800
C) ₦3,000
D) ₦5,200
Answer: a
Solution: Net profit for Department P = Sales ₦6 000 – Cost of Goods Sold [(₂₀₀₀ + ₦2 500 + ₦300 – ₦1 500) = ₦3 300] – Expenses ₦200 = ₦2 500.

Q: The rent expense for Trendy store is ₦3500. Trendy store has three departments; jewelry, hair dressing, and clothing. The floor spaces occupied by the departments are 3:2:5 respectively. What is the rent allocated to clothing department?
A) ₦700
B) ₦1050
C)  ₦1750
D) ₦3500
Answer: c
Solution: Jewelry 3/10 x 3500 = 1050

Hairdressing 2/10 x 3500 = 700

Clothing 5/10 x 3500 = 1750

Q: Calls in advance are treated in the balance sheet as_______
A) Current asset
B) Fixed asset
C) Current liability
D) Fixed liability
Answer: c
Solution: calls in advance is treated as a current liability until the calls are made and the amount actually becomes payable by the shareholders

Q: When goodwill is not retained in the business, the entries in the new partners books will be to debit______________

A) Goodwill account and credit partners capital account
B) Cash account and credit goodwill account
C) Goodwill account and credit cash account
D)  Partners capital account and credit goodwill account
Answer: d
Solution: When goodwill is not retained in the business, it means the goodwill account is written off immediately after being created. This involves a two-step process:
Step 1: Create goodwill

Debit: Goodwill Account
Credit: Partners' Capital Accounts (in profit-sharing ratio)

Step 2: Write off goodwill (since it's not retained)

Debit: Partners' Capital Accounts (in new profit-sharing ratio)
Credit: Goodwill Account

The net effect in the new partners' books is:

Debit: Partners' Capital Account
Credit: Goodwill Account

This represents the partners absorbing the goodwill write-off through their capital accounts rather than keeping it as an asset on the books.

Q: Which of the following should not be adjusted for in the profit and loss account?
A) Accruals
B) inventory
C) subscription
D) depreciation
Answer: c
Solution: is adjusted for in the income and expenditure account

Q: Tea and Cup are into a partnership business. Interests on drawings made by partners are at 10% per annum. Tea’s capital is ₦70000 and current balance is ₦50000. He withdrew the following amounts during the year : 3000 on 31st January , 2000 on 31st March, 4000 on 1st July, 1500 on the 30th September, 2500 on 1st November. Cup’s capital is ₦100000 and current balance is ₦40000. He made no drawings during the period. what is the closing balance in Tea’s current account
A) 36,925Cr
B)  40,000Cr
C) 50,000Dr
D)  36,295Dr
Answer: d
Solution: Starting with Tea’s opening credit balance of ₦50 000, we subtract his total drawings (₦3 000 + 2 000 + 4 000 + 1 500 + 2 500 = ₦13 000) and the interest on those drawings (₦3 000×10%×11/12 + ₦2 000×10%×9/12 + ₦4 000×10%×6/12 + ₦1 500×10%×3/12 + ₦2 500×10%×2/12 ≈ ₦705), giving:

Closing current balance = ₦50000 − ₦13000 − ₦705 = ₦36295

Q: Ade, Tony, Rose share profit and losses in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 1 respectively. Ade retires and the remaining partners decide to take Ade’s share in the existing ratio. What is the new ratio?

A) 1 : 1
B) 3 : 6
C) 2 : 1
D) 2 : 6
Answer: c
Solution: When Ade’s 3‑part share is divided between Tony and Rose in their 2 : 1 ratio, Tony receives 3 × (2/3) = 2 parts and Rose receives 3 × (1/3) = 1 part, so Tony’s total becomes 2 + 2 = 4 and Rose’s becomes 1 + 1 = 2, giving a new ratio of 4 : 2 (i.e. 2 : 1).

Q: Branch stock adjustment account is prepared at?
A) Cost price
B)  new price
C) invoice price
D) normal price
Answer: c
Solution: Branch stock adjustment account deals with the loading on the respective items of goods relating to Branch stock account.

Branch adjustment account is prepared at invoice price.

 The difference between the two sides of this account reveals either gross profit (if credit side is greater than the debit side) or gross loss (if debit side is greater than the credit side).

Q: Why are adjustments in the profit and loss account necessary?
A) To cover some expenses of the following year
B) To show the provisions made during the year
C) To show the total expenses paid and income received during the year
D) To ascertain the actual expenses incurred and income earned during the year
Answer: d
Solution: Fundamental principle of preparing P&L account is that expenses and income relating to only the trading period are taken to the trading profit and loss account.

Q: A business has the following balance sheet as at the beginning of the year: Capital ₦40,000, Furnishing ₦10,000, Ceiling Fan ₦1,500, and Cash in Hand ₦28,500, with total assets and liabilities both equaling ₦40,000.
During the year ending 31/1/95, the following transactions occurred:

Rent for shop ₦12,000 paid for the year
Total purchases ₦15,000
Total sales ₦8,200
Stock of goods left ₦10,000
Paid sales boy ₦500

What is the new balance sheet total as at 31/1/95?
A)  ₦39,700
B)  ₦40,000
C)  ₦41,500
D) ₦48,500
Answer: a
Solution: Starting with opening cash of ₦28,500, we track cash movements:
Cash Outflows:

Rent paid: ₦12,000
Purchases: ₦15,000
Sales boy wages: ₦500
Total outflows: ₦27,500

Cash Inflows:

Sales: ₦8,200

New Cash Balance: ₦28,500 - ₦27,500 + ₦8,200 = ₦9,200
New Balance Sheet:

Assets: Furnishing ₦10,000 + Ceiling Fan ₦1,500 + Stock ₦10,000 + Cash ₦9,200 = ₦30,700
Capital: ₦40,000 - ₦300 (net loss) = ₦39,700
Prepaid Rent: ₦9,000 (11 months remaining)

New Balance Sheet Total: ₦39,700

Q: In the absence of a partnership deed, the act stipulates that____________
A) An amount should be fixed as salaries for partners
B) Profits and losses should not be shared equally
C) Interest on partner’s loan should be 25%
D) Interest should not be allowed on partners drawings
Answer: d
Solution: Under the Partnership Act, the following rules will be applied in the absence of an agreement among partners:

  i. Profit or losses of the firm will be shared equally by the partners

  ii. Interest on capital will not be allowed to any partner.

  iii. No interest will be charged on drawings

  iv. Interest on loan will be 6% on the loan

  v. No salary or remuneration will be allowed to any of the partners

  vi. Every partner must take part in the management of the partnership business

  vii. The partnership books are kept at the place of business of the partnership and every partner may have access to and inspect and copy any of them.

Q: Cost of rent as an expense can be apportioned to all department on the basis of:
A) No of employees
B) stock value
C) space occupied
D) wages
Answer: c
Solution: Indirect expenses are allocated among departments in order to ascertain the profits or loss made by each department

Q: When goods are sent to branch at cost plus mark up, it means that the branch should sell at_____________
A) Price above or below the stipulated price
B) Any price but not below the transfer price
C) Cost price
D) A price that is equal to the mark up
Answer: a
Solution: Cost plus mark up is a pricing strategy in which the selling price is determined by adding a specific amount mark up to a product unit cost

Q: In dealing with incomplete record, fixed assets are posted to___________-

A) Profit and loss account as brought forward figure
B) Closing balance sheet as carried forward figure
C) Closing balance sheet as brought forward figure
D) Profit and loss as carried forward figure
Answer: d
Solution: fixed asset are brought forward in closing balance sheet

Q: The cost price method is applicable when_____
A) Goods are sold at specific prices
B)  goods are perishable
C)  goods attract different gross profit percentage
D) to disclose gross profit or loss
Answer: b
Solution: cost price method is used to enhance quick sales

Q: Sule and Ahmed are in partnership sharing profit and losses equally. If Khadija is admitted as a new partner to take 1/5 th as her share. What is the new profit or loss sharing?
A)  Sule1/3, Ahmed1/3, Khadija 1/3
B) Sule1/3, Ahmed1/3, Khadija 1/3
C) Sule1/5, Ahmed1/5, Khadija3/5
D)  Sule2/5, Ahmed1/5, Khadija2/5
Answer: b
Solution: If Khadija is to take 1/5th i.e. 20%

  Sule and Ahmed are to share 80% (100% - 20%) equally

  Sule = 2/5

  Ahmed = 2/5

  Khadija = 1/5

Q: Adex Ltd. issues stock to its retail branches at cost price. The following information relates to Ede branch: Stock at branch 1st January at cost ₦400, Goods sent to branch at cost ₦8000, Returns to head office ₦340, Cash sales ₦9160, Stock at branch 31st December at cost ₦720. Calculate the cost of goods credited to the head office trading account.
A) ₦7340
B)  ₦7460
C)  ₦7500
D) ₦7660
Answer: a
Solution: The cost of goods credited to the Head Office Trading Account is computed as:

Opening stock (₦400)

Goods sent to branch (₦8,000)
– Returns to Head Office (₦340)
– Closing stock (₦720)
= ₦7,340

Q: Which of the following is not a type of branch?
A) Dependent branch
B) foreign branch
C) independent branch
D) single branch
Answer: d
Solution: Branches are typically classified as:

Dependent branches, which rely on the head office for purchases and policies

Independent branches, which operate like standalone entities with their own accounting systems

Foreign branches, which are located in another country and may involve additional currency and regulatory considerations

The term “single branch” isn’t used as a formal classification.

papers.sourceText: Q: The acid test ratio in the company is A) 1:1 B) 1:2 C) 2:3 D) 3:2 Answer: a Solution: To find the acid test ratio (quick ratio), calculate Quick Assets divided by Current Liabilities. Quick Assets (Current Assets minus Stock): Cash: ₦8,000 Debtors: ₦6,000 Less: Stock: ₦4,000 (excluded as it's not easily convertible to cash) Total Quick Assets: ₦14,000 Current Liabilities: Creditors: ₦9,000 Accrued wages: ₦5,000 Total Current Liabilities: ₦14,000 Acid Test Ratio: Quick Assets : Current Liabilities = ₦14,000 : ₦14,000 = 1:1 Q: Shares of N3 nominal value were issued at a price of N4. The difference of N1 is a A) commission. B) discount. C) premium. D) bonus. Answer: c Q: A debit balance of Nl50,000 in a cash account shows that A) cash has been overspent by N150,000 B) there was N150,000 cash in hand C) the total of cash received was less than N150,000 D) N150,000 was the total of cash paid out. Answer: b Q: Which type of cashbook entry involves recording the same amount on both the debit and credit sides to offset each other? A) Contra entry B) Compound entry C) Transfer entry D) Journal entry Answer: a Solution: A contra entry in the cashbook is used when the business moves money between its own cash and bank accounts—such as depositing cash into the bank or withdrawing cash from the bank Q: Ade, Tony, Rose share profit and losses in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 1 respectively. Ade retires and the remaining partners decide to take Ade’s share in the existing ratio. What is the new ratio? A) 1 : 1 B) 3 : 6 C) 2 : 1 D) 2 : 6 Answer: c Solution: When Ade’s 3‑part share is divided between Tony and Rose in their 2 : 1 ratio, Tony receives 3 × (2/3) = 2 parts and Rose receives 3 × (1/3) = 1 part, so Tony’s total becomes 2 + 2 = 4 and Rose’s becomes 1 + 1 = 2, giving a new ratio of 4 : 2 (i.e. 2 : 1). Q: A petty cash fund is: A) Used to pay relatively small amount B) reimbursed when the amount of money in the fund is reduced to a predetermined minimum amount C) Established by estimating the amount of cash needed for disbursement of relatively small amount during a specified period D) All of the above Answer: d Q: The act of making necessary adjustment after comparing the actual cost with targeted cost is cost ---------------------------- A) conversion B) control C) allocation D) analysis Answer: b Solution: The process of reviewing actual costs against targeted (or budgeted) costs and then making the necessary corrective adjustments is known as cost control. Q: Using the following information, calculate the balance that should appear on the bank statement. The cashbook shows a balance of ₦13,560. There are unpresented cheques totaling ₦5,120, and a cheque for ₦2,300 has been paid into the bank but not yet credited. The bank has also received a dividend of ₦2,000, charged ₦280 in bank fees, and processed a standing order of ₦600. A) ₦10,740 B) ₦11,860 C) ₦16,380 D) ₦17,500 Answer: d Solution: Balance per bank statement = ₦13,560 + ₦5,120 + ₦2,000 – ₦2,300 – ₦280 – ₦600 = ₦17,500. Q: If a promoter pays a lawyer ₦5,000 for services rendered in preparing a Memorandum of Incorporation, the journal entry is to debit? A) preliminary expenses, credit cash accounts B) promoter, credit creditors' accounts C) lawyer's credit cash accounts D) cash , credit incorporation accounts Answer: a Solution: When a promoter pays ₦5,000 to a lawyer for preparing a Memorandum of Incorporation, it's considered a pre-incorporation expense (also called preliminary expenses), since it's incurred before the company is officially formed. Q: In a cash book, the opening balance was ₦7,600, closing balance ₦9,200 and the total cash received during the period was ₦18,000. What was the amount of cash paid out during the period? A) ₦8,900 B) ₦9,800 C) ₦14,600 D) ₦16,400 Answer: d Solution: sing the cash book equation: Opening balance + Receipts − Payments = Closing balance Rearrange for payments: Payments = Opening + Receipts − Closing = ₦7,600 + ₦18,000 − ₦9,200 = ₦16,400 Q: Use the information below to answer this question. Dangote acquired Dantata’s business for ₦350,000. The total asset work were ₦820,000 and liabilities amounted to ₦ 640,000 The double entry to record the goodwill in the books is debt A) purchase of business account and credit cash account B) goodwill account and credit purchase of business account C) cash account and credit goodwill account D) goodwill account and credit cash account Answer: b Solution: when there is excess of purchase consideration over net assets, the accounting entries is to debit goodwill account as the receiving account and credit purchase of business account as the giving account. Q: Where the debit side of the income and expenditure account is higher than the credit side, the difference is A) deficit B) surplus C) gain D) loss Answer: a Q: Which of the following is used to update the cash book in bank reconciliation? A) Interest received and unpresented cheques B) Commission and debit note C) Unpresented cheques and direct credit D) Interest received and direct credit Answer: d Solution: Reason: those are items shown on the bank statement but not yet recorded in the cash book, so you update the cash book with them. Unpresented cheques are recorded in the cash book already and are used to reconcile to the bank statement (not to update the cash book). Q: The effect of transaction when cash is paid into the bank is? A) bank balance decrease and cash balance increase B) cash balance decrease and bank balance increase C) bank balance decrease and cash balance decrease D) cash balance increase and bank balance increase Answer: b Solution: When cash is paid into the bank, the cash balance decreases because you are taking cash out of your possession and depositing it into the bank. On the other hand, your bank balance increases because you are adding money to your bank account. Therefore, the effect of the transaction is that the cash balance decreases and the bank balance increases. Q: Use the information below to answer questions 49 and 50 Given PTF Trial balance (Extract) as at 31 December 1999 showing: Cash ₦2,000 (Dr), Investments ₦3,000 (Dr), Accounts receivable ₦6,000 (Dr), and Fund balance ₦11,000 (Cr). Assuming all the investments realized ₦4m, what will be the ending fund balance? A) ₦8m B) ₦12,000 C) ₦13m D) ₦16m Answer: b Solution: Step 1: Calculate gain/loss on investments Cost of investments (from trial balance): ₦3,000 Realization value: ₦4,000 Gain on disposal = ₦4,000 - ₦3,000 = ₦1,000 Step 2: Calculate ending fund balance Opening fund balance: ₦11,000 Add: Gain on disposal of investments: ₦1,000 Ending fund balance = ₦11,000 + ₦1,000 = ₦12,000 Q: What is the net profit? A) N 46,000 B) N 45,000 C) N 28,000 D) N 27,000 Answer: c Q: A business acquisition shows the following assets and liabilities: Plant and Machinery ₦190,000, Motor Vehicle ₦170,000, Stock ₦60,000, Current Liabilities ₦50,000, Purchase consideration ₦400,000. Determine the amount of goodwill. A) ₦110 000 B) ₦80 000 C) ₦90 000 D) ₦30 000 Answer: d Solution: Net assets acquired = (₦190,000 + ₦170,000 + ₦60,000) – ₦50,000 = ₦420,000 – ₦50,000 = ₦370,000 Goodwill = Purchase consideration – Net assets = ₦400,000 – ₦370,000 = ₦30,000. Q: The journal is a book A) of primary entry into which all transactions are entered before posting B) kept by journalist for reporting events C) of prime entry into which postings are made from the ledger D) of analyzing major accounts Answer: a Q: Which of the following accounting conventions suggests that accountants should use a method of valuation that understates rather than overstates results? A) monetary B) cost C) conservatism D) historical Answer: c Solution: The conservatism convention (also known as prudence) suggests that accountants should use methods of valuation that understate rather than overstate results Q: How much is sundry expenses? A) N 2 700 B) N 2,250 C) N1,550 D) N2000. Answer: a Q: A petty cash account has an imprest of D28,000. The account has a debit balance of D5.000. How much cash is needed to restore the imprest? A) D33,000 B) D28,000 C) D23,000 D) D5,000 Answer: c Q: Responsibility accounting is particularly concerned with? A) histoical accounting B) controllable costs C) storekeeping D) valuation of stock Answer: b Solution: Responsibility accounting is a system of accounting that: Identifies areas of responsibility within an organization (e.g., departments, units, or managers), Measures the performance of those areas, and Holds the responsible managers accountable for the costs and revenues they can control. Q: Prepaid expenses is an item in A) Fixed Asset B) Current Asset C) Liabilities D) Long term liabilities Answer: b Q: One of the items listed below will not be found in a company’s memorandum and article of association. Which is it? A) objects and their alteration B) location of business C) bank signatories D) powers of directors Answer: c Solution: The memorandum of association is the document that sets up the company and the articles of association set out how the company is run, governed and owned. The articles of association includes the responsibilities and powers of the directors and the means by which the members exert control over the board of directors. The MOA of a company contains the object for which the company is formed. It identifies the scope of its operations and determines the boundaries it cannot cross. Q: When expenses are paid on behalf of the venture, the accounting entries is to debit A) bank account and credit joint venture account B) expenses account and credit bank account C) joint venture account and credit expenses account D) joint venture account and credit bank account Answer: d Solution: Joint venture account is an account that all expenditure incurred for the venture is debited and all income is credited to. Debit joint venture and credit bank account because expenses incurred on behalf of the venture has to be debited to the joint venture account and since the money is joint out the bank must be credited to balance the account Q: Profit or loss in a partnership is usually arrived at after deducting from gross profit all expenses including? A) partners' salaries B) interest on capital C) partners' drawings D) interest on loans Answer: d Solution: Explanation: Profit or loss is found after deducting operating expenses (e.g., rent, wages, interest on loans). Items like partners' drawings are not expenses, and partners' salaries or interest on capital are typically treated as appropriations of profit (handled in the profit & loss appropriation account), not ordinary business expenses. Q: Bank reconciliation statement reconciles A) bank and cash balances in the cash book B) bank balance in the cash book and bank statement balance C) cash balance in the cash book and bank statement balance D) bank balance brought down and bank balance carried down in the cash bcok. Answer: b Q: In Manufacturing Account, prime cost plus factory overhead is known as A) conversion cost B) cost of raw materials consumed C) total cost D) production cost Answer: d Q: Given: Capital ₦200,000, Liabilities ₦10,000, Total assets ₦210,000. If the business is purchased at a price including a goodwill of ₦20,000, what must have been the purchase price? A) ₦190,000 B) ₦210,000 C) ₦220,000 D) ₦230,000. Answer: c Solution: Step 1: Calculate the net worth of the business Net Worth = Total Assets - Total Liabilities Net Worth = ₦210,000 - ₦10,000 = ₦200,000 (This also equals the Capital as shown: ₦200,000) Step 2: Calculate the purchase price Purchase Price = Net Worth + Goodwill Purchase Price = ₦200,000 + ₦20,000 = ₦220,000 Q: Determine the amount provided for discount allowed on debtors. A) N 1 000 B) N 3000 C) N 900 D) N1500. Answer: a Q: The records of Superstores shows a loan of ₦14,000 from Bala,creditor ₦8,000 and assets ₦190,500. What is the firm's capital? A) ₦184, 000 B) ₦196,500 C) ₦212,000 D) ₦168,500 Answer: d Solution: The net working capital formula is calculated by subtracting the current liabilities from the current assets. Assets = 190,500 liabilities = 14,000 + 8,000 = 22,000 190,500 - 22,000 = 168,000 (capital) Q: A book that contains the accounts for the financial transactions of an organization is the A) journal B) ledger C) folio D) register Answer: b Q: The balance at the end of the period is A) 270,000. B) 139,000. C) 131,000. D) 120,000. Answer: c Q: Use the information below to answer questions 27 to 28 Purchase:..Raw materials.................₦15 000 Finished goods...........................₦11 400 Stock:....(1/7/01)Raw materials..........₦2 250 Work-in-progress.........................₦1 875 Wages:.....Direct........................₦17 100 Indirect.................................₦5 400 Stock:.....(30/06/02)Raw materials.......₦3 000 Work-in-progress.........................₦3 375 What is the cost of manufactured goods? A) ₦49 125 B) ₦48 750 C) ₦37 625 D) ₦35 250 Answer: d Solution: Raw materials consumed = Opening RM + Purchases RM − Closing RM = ₦2,250 + ₦15,000 − ₦3,000 = ₦14,250 Direct labour = ₦17,100 Manufacturing overheads (indirect wages) = ₦5,400 Total manufacturing costs = RM consumed + Direct labour + Overheads = ₦14,250 + ₦17,100 + ₦5,400 = ₦36,750 Add: Opening WIP = ₦1,875 → ₦38,625 Less: Closing WIP = ₦3,375 → ₦35,250 Final answer: Cost of manufactured goods = ₦35,250. Q: A business has the following balance sheet: Capital ₦40,000, Furnishing ₦10,000, Ceiling Fan ₦1,500, and Cash in Hand ₦28,500, with total assets and liabilities both equaling ₦40,000. If at 31/1/95 the following information was ascertained: Rent for shop ₦12,000 paid for the year Total purchases ₦15,000 Total sales ₦8,200 Stock of goods left ₦10,000 Paid sales boy ₦500 What is the balance on its cash account as at 31/1/95? A) ₦22,800 B) ₦9,200 C) ₦800 D) ₦21,200 Answer: b Solution: Starting with opening cash balance of ₦28,500, we calculate the cash movements: Cash Outflows: Rent paid: ₦12,000 Purchases: ₦15,000 Sales boy wages: ₦500 Total cash outflows: ₦27,500 Cash Inflows: Sales (assuming cash sales): ₦8,200 Cash Balance Calculation: Opening Cash + Cash Inflows - Cash Outflows = ₦28,500 + ₦8,200 - ₦27,500 = ₦36,700 - ₦27,500 = ₦9,200 The cash account balance as at 31/1/95 is ₦9,200. Q: Use the information below to answer this question: i. cash at bank ii. cash in hand iii. premises iv. land v. creditors vi. loan from friends/bank What are the current assets? A) i and v B) i and ii C) ii and iv D) iii and v Answer: b Solution: Current assets are short‑term assets expected to be converted into cash within one year. From the list, cash at bank and cash in hand are the current assets. Q: (i) Meet growth and diversification need. (ii) Reach out to particular customers or markets (iii) Comply with some regulatory directives (iv) Increase employees' income. Which of the reasons above do companies consider in establishing branches? A) i and ii B) i, ii and iii C) ii, iii and iv D) iii and iv Answer: b Solution: Companies typically establish branches to support strategic objectives such as expanding operations, targeting new customer segments, or meeting legal/regulatory requirements, not simply to boost employee earnings. That means they consider: Meet growth and diversification needs Reach out to particular customers or markets Comply with some regulatory directives They do not set up branches primarily to increase employees’ income. Q: From the Sales Ledger Control Account shown, which displays various transactions including: Balance brought forward of ₦3,250, Sales of ₦19,075, Dishonoured cheque of ₦625, Stopped cheque of ₦250, and Balance carried down of ₦230 on the debit side; and Balance brought forward of ₦215, Bank of ₦16,387.50, Discount of ₦862.50, Returns inwards of ₦325, Set off of ₦900, and Balance carried down of ₦4,740 on the credit side, with both sides totaling ₦23,430. The amount ₦16,378.50 described as "Bank" represents what? A) receipts from trade debtors only B) cash sales for the month including discount C) receipts from all debtors of the business D) cash sales for the month excluding discount Answer: a Solution: In a Sales Ledger Control Account, the "Bank" entry on the credit side specifically represents cash received from trade debtors (customers who owed money from credit sales). Q: The double entry required for the mark-up is debit Branch A) Sales Account, credit Branch Adjustment Account B) Adjustment Account, credit Branch Stock Account C) Stock Account, credit Branch Adjustment Account D) Profit and Loss Account, credit Branch Stock Account, Answer: c Q: Use the information below to answer questions 15 and 16 Calculate the value of fixed assets A) ₦17,052 B) ₦18469 C) ₦27 001 D) ₦27051 Answer: a Solution: Fixed assets: Land & building = ₦8,470 Furniture & fittings = ₦5,120 Motor vehicles = ₦3,462 Total fixed assets = 8,470 + 5,120 + 3,462 = ₦17,052
