Q: Discount received is charge to
A) current account
B) profit and loss
C) rading account
D) balance sheet
Answer: b
Solution: Discount received is treated as income to the business hence it is credited to the profit and loss.

Q: The importance of bank statement is all except
A)  verifies the accuracy of balances of cash book and cheque book
B) helps to detect and rectify any error
C)  helps to debit an account
D)  helps to update the cash book
Answer: c
Solution: Bank statement is prepared by the bank to an account border showing the transactions between the customer and the bank within a period of time. It is usually issued monthly or at agreed intervals to the customers.

Q: An ordinary share of ₦100 was issued at ₦80. The share was issued at
A) premium
B) par
C) discount
D) loss
Answer: c
Solution: Share issued at discount is a situation whereby shares are quoted below the nominal value.

Q: The advantage of double entry is that
A)  it is easy to prepare the final account
B)  it increase assets
C) has cash and bank column
D) It disburses cash
Answer: a
Solution: Double-entry accounting is easy to prepare and helps guarantee accurate financial records by revealing data entry errors. Double-entry accounting provides a complete record of financial transactions for a business.

Q: Given the following manufacturing information: stock of finished goods on January 1st was ₦50,640 and on December 31st was ₦71,380; stock of raw materials on January 1st was ₦32,160 and on December 31st was ₦29,640; purchase of raw materials was ₦145,000; manufacturing wages were ₦52,000; depreciation on factory equipment was ₦16,500; direct expenses were ₦12,500; factory fuel cost ₦7,000; and carriage inwards on raw materials was ₦7,000, What is the Total Prime Cost?
A) ₦220,480
B) ₦219,020
C) ₦200,480
D) ₦190,000
Answer: b
Solution: Total Prime Cost:
Prime Cost = Cost of Raw Materials Consumed + Manufacturing Wages + Direct Expenses
Prime Cost = ₦154,520 + ₦52,000 + ₦12,500 = ₦219,020

Q: The purpose of profit and loss account is to ascertain
A) Gross profit
B) Capital
C) Expenses
D) Net profit
Answer: d
Solution: The profit and loss account also known as Income statement is prepared to ascertain the net profit. The net profit is ascertain when the expenses is deducted from the Gross Profit.

Q: A statement in a double-entry system in which are recorded all the transactions of one specific class, which takes place during the period is called
A) Double entry system
B) Ledger
C) Cash Book
D) Petty Cash Book
Answer: b
Solution: A ledger is a separate record within the general ledger that is assigned to a specific asset, liability, equity item, revenue type, or expense type. Examples of ledger accounts are: Cash, Accounts receivable.

Q: Given the following information: additional capital is ₦4,000, capital is ₦8,000, closing capital is ₦12,000, and net profit is ₦1,500, what are the drawings for the period?
A) ₦1,500
B) ₦3,000
C) ₦12,000
D) ₦10,500
Answer: a
Solution: To find the drawings, use the capital account equation:
Opening Capital + Additional Capital + Net Profit - Drawings = Closing Capital
Rearranging to find drawings:
Drawings = Opening Capital + Additional Capital + Net Profit - Closing Capital
From the given information:

Opening Capital = ₦8,000
Additional Capital = ₦4,000
Net Profit = ₦1,500
Closing Capital = ₦12,000

Drawings = ₦8,000 + ₦4,000 + ₦1,500 - ₦12,000
Drawings = ₦13,500 - ₦12,000 = ₦1,500
Therefore, the drawings for the period stand at ₦1,500.

Q: Goods can be charged to branches using any of these pricing methods except
A)  cost price
B) cost plus percentage
C)  selling price
D)  selling plus percentage
Answer: d
Solution: There are three different pricing methods which are used for charging goods to branches.
They are:
1. At cost price
2. At cost plus a percentage
3. At selling price.

Q: Using the same information extracted from the books of Miliki state where sinking of bore holes cost ₦2,900,000, purchase of motor car ₦920,000, stationery ₦300,000, electricity ₦45,000, purchase of drugs ₦76,000, and purchase of beds ₦425,000, what is the capital expenditure?
A)  ₦345,000
B) ₦3,245,000
C) ₦421,000
D)  ₦4,245,000
Answer: d
Solution: Capital expenditure refers to spending on long-term assets that will benefit the organization for more than one year. These are investments in fixed assets.
From the given items:

Sinking of bore holes: ₦2,900,000 (capital - infrastructure development)
Purchase of motor car: ₦920,000 (capital - fixed asset)
Purchase of beds: ₦425,000 (capital - durable equipment)

Capital expenditure = ₦2,900,000 + ₦920,000 + ₦425,000 = ₦4,245,000
Therefore, the capital expenditure is ₦4,245,000.

Q: Given:
Ordinary share dividend ₦100,000, General reserve ₦4,100, Net profit b/d ₦27,370, corporation tax ₦2,500, Profit and loss ₦28,200, Interim ordinary dividend ₦4,050, Goodwill 20,50 provide for preference Dividend ₦2100 and Final ordinary Dividend of 5% and also write off Goodwill at ₦1500.
The retained profit in the Appropriation account is
A)  ₦55,570
B) ₦36,320
C)  ₦50,000
D) ₦30,000
Answer: b
Solution: Ordinary share dividend = 5% × 10,000 = 5000
Retained profit = (27,370 + 28,000 - 4100 + 1500 - 4050 + 5000 + 2100 + 2500)
⇒ 55,570 - 19,250 = ₦36,320

Q: The following information were extracted from the books of Miliki state: sinking of bore holes ₦2,900,000, purchase of motor car ₦920,000, stationery ₦300,000, electricity ₦45,000, purchase of drugs ₦76,000, and purchase of beds ₦425,000. What is the recurrent expenditure?
A)  ₦345,000
B) ₦3,245,000
C) ₦421,000
D) ₦4,245,000
Answer: c
Solution: Recurrent expenditure refers to operating expenses that occur regularly and are consumed within a short period (usually within a year). These are expenses for day-to-day operations.
From the given items:

Stationery: ₦300,000 (recurrent - office supplies)
Electricity: ₦45,000 (recurrent - utility expense)
Purchase of drugs: ₦76,000 (recurrent - medical supplies)

The other items (sinking of bore holes, motor car, and beds) are capital expenditures as they are long-term assets.
Recurrent expenditure = ₦300,000 + ₦45,000 + ₦76,000 = ₦421,000
Therefore, the recurrent expenditure is ₦421,000.

Q: The two recognised accounting bases are
A) cash and credit
B)  personal and impersonal
C) Accrual and Cash
D) Drawings and Private
Answer: c
Solution: Accounting bases are the totality of method adopted by an enterprises for applying fundamental accounting concepts to its Financial transactions. However, the two bases are cash and Accrual basis

Q: Based on the final accounts of Wazobi Ventures for the year ended 30th June, 1998, where sales were ₦233,000 and cost of goods sold was ₦170,000, with overhead expenses including admin expenses of ₦16,800, selling expenses of ₦15,000, and other overhead expenses of ₦6,200, resulting in a net profit of ₦25,000, Calculate the net profit on percentage of expenses.
A) 60%
B) 25%
C) 13%
D) 65.70%
Answer: d
Solution: Total Expenses = Admin expenses + Selling expenses + Other overhead expenses
Total Expenses = ₦16,800 + ₦15,000 + ₦6,200 = ₦38,000
Net Profit as % of Expenses = (Net Profit ÷ Total Expenses) × 100
Net Profit as % of Expenses = (₦25,000 ÷ ₦38,000) × 100 = 65.7%

Q: Abelawo ltd operates a retail branch at Aba. All purchases are made by the head office in Onitsha and goods are charged to the branch at cost plus 50%. During the year ended. Goods sent to branch at invoiced price is ₦30,870, cash sales ₦13,020 and Bad debt amounted to 129. From the following, what is the profit?
A) ₦20,580
B) ₦10,290
C) ₦7,980
D) ₦30,870
Answer: b
Solution: To find the profit, the unrealized profit in the goods sent to branch needs to be determined.
Given information:

Goods sent to branch at invoiced price = ₦30,870
Invoiced price = Cost + 50% markup
Cash sales = ₦13,020
Bad debt = ₦129

Finding the cost price of goods sent to branch:
If invoiced price = Cost + 50% of cost = 1.5 × Cost
Then: Cost = ₦30,870 ÷ 1.5 = ₦20,580
Unrealized profit in goods sent to branch:
Profit = Invoiced price - Cost price
Profit = ₦30,870 - ₦20,580 = ₦10,290
The profit from the markup on goods sent to branch is ₦10,290.

Q: Which of these will not appear in the preparation of control account.
I. Bad debts
II. Discounts
III. Returns
IV. Provision for bad debts
A) I only
B) II and III
C) I and III only
D) IV only
Answer: d
Solution: Provision for bad debts and trade discount allowed will not appear in the account.

Q: Ojo, Sam and Ade are in partnership sharing profit in the ratio 4:3:1 respectively. From their books for the year ended, interest on drawings and capital is allowed at 5% respectively, and profit for the year amounted to ₦4,950. What is Ojo's share of profit?
A) ₦7,000
B) ₦2,475
C) ₦3,000
D) ₦991.8
Answer: b
Solution: To find Ojo's share of profit:
The profit sharing ratio is 4:3:1 (Ojo : Sam : Ade)
Total ratio = 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 parts
Ojo's share = (4/8) × Total Profit
Ojo's share = (4/8) × ₦4,950
Ojo's share = (1/2) × ₦4,950
Ojo's share = ₦2,475
Therefore, Ojo's share of profit is ₦2,475.

Q: Use the following to answer this question.
Industry ltd, issued 100,000 shares at ₦1 each out of its Authorized share capital of ₦200,000 at ₦1 each. At the of the first call, all shareholders paid in full, except for two shareholder who owes ₦20,000.

The company's paid-up capital is
A) ₦70,000
B)  ₦80,000
C) ₦220,000
D)  ₦120,000
Answer: b
Solution: Paid up capital is the total amount paid up or credited as paid up, on the issued share capital.
From the question above, the issued share capital is ₦100,000 and two of the shareholder owes ₦20,000. Therefore, the paid up is 100,000 - 20,000 = ₦80,000.

Q: The method of stock valuation in which the issue price is obtained by dividing the value of stock in hand by unit of stock in hand is
A) FIFO
B) LIFO
C) SAP
D) WAP
Answer: d
Solution: Weighted Average Price (WAP): Under this method issues are priced at a weighted average price which is obtained by dividing the value by the unit of stock in hand. Issues will continue to be priced at this price until a new batch is received when a new weighted Average price is calculated.

Q: Ojo, Sam and Ade are in partnership sharing profit in the ratio 4:3:1 respectively. From their books for the year ended, interest on drawings and capital is allowed at 5% respectively, and profit for the year amounted to ₦4,950. Given that Ojo has capital of ₦5,000, Sam has capital of ₦4,000, and Ade has capital of ₦6,000, what is the interest on capital for Ade?
A) ₦250
B) ₦200
C) ₦300
D) ₦400
Answer: c
Solution: Interest on Capital for Ade = Capital Balance × Interest Rate
Interest on Capital for Ade = ₦6,000 × 5% = ₦300

Q: Retained profits is an example of
A)  Revenue reserve
B)  Capital reserves
C) General reserves
D) Loan capital
Answer: a
Solution: Retained profit is part of the part of the profits of an organization not distributed as dividends but ploughed back into the business for expansion.

Q: Majority of commercial transactions are termed credit transactions, which means
A) The buyers pay immediately for goods bought
B) Settlement is deferred to a future date
C) No account will be opened
D) Item of expenditure increases
Answer: b
Solution: In credit transactions, the transfer of ownership takes place before payment to the supplier i.e settlement is at a future safe.

Q: The rules of double entry states that
A)  for every debit entry, there must be a corresponding debit entry
B)  for every credit entry, there must be a corresponding credit entry
C) all transactions must be recorded in two accounts, one account is debited and another is credited
D) all transaction must be credited
Answer: c
Solution: Double entry system is the entry of debit and credit for each transaction in the ledger. Hence the double entry rules states that "debit the receivers, credit the giver".

Q: Based on the Receipts and Payment Account extract showing: balance brought forward ₦3,650, subscription ₦7,500 less ₦2,000 equals ₦1,000, fees ₦8,500, insurance ₦900, rate ₦11,700, and balance carried down ₦8,050, with totals of ₦20,650 on both sides, and given the following additional information as at 1st January 1999 and 31st December 1999 respectively: rates owing ₦3,600 and ₦2,000, insurance prepaid ₦50 and ₦1,000, subscription in arrears ₦700 and ₦600, The figure ₦1000 represent what in the balance sheet.
A) Assets
B) Liability
C) capital
D) Subscription
Answer: b
Solution: The figure ₦1,000 represents B. Liability in the balance sheet.
This ₦1,000 is derived from ₦7,500 (total cash received for subscriptions) minus ₦2,000 (subscription received in advance). The ₦2,000 that was deducted represents money received from members for future periods, creating an obligation to provide services later. This makes it a liability on the balance sheet - specifically "subscription received in advance" or "deferred subscription income."

Q: Transactions are recorded or posted to the ledger in line with
A) Accounting Concept
B) Source document
C)  Double Entry Principle
D) Data collection
Answer: c
Solution: The main principle of double-entry system is that for every debit there is a corresponding credit for an equal amount of money and for every credit there is a corresponding debit for an equal amount of money; i.e. for every transaction one account is debited for, the amount of transaction and the other account is also credited. 

Q: Goods were purchased for resale on credit costing ₦150,000 on 30th September 2008 from Tosanwumi International. The entry to record these transaction is debit
A)  Tosanwumi International, credit purchase Account
B) Purchase Account ₦150,000, credit Tosanwumi International Account ₦150,000
C) Credit Account ₦150,000, Credit Tosanwumi International ₦150,000
D) Tosanwumi International ₦150,000, credit credit Account ₦150,000
Answer: b
Solution: When a purchase was made, a credit purchase invoice would have been issued by the supplier, Tosanwumi International, which would be signed by Mr. Roi as evidence of his acceptance of liability to pay for the goods.

The two accounts needed to record this transaction are the purchase Account and Tosanwumi International Account. purchase account would be debited while the Tosanwumi International Account credited.

Q: Show how the following transaction will be recorded applying the double-entry principle:
Rent ₦50,000 was paid by Mr. Roi to his landlord on 1st July 2017 by cheque.
A)  Dr Rent A/c; Dr Bank A/c
B)  Dr Bank A/c; Cr Rent A/c
C) Dr Rent A/c; Cr Bank A/c
D) Dr Rent A/c; Cr Mr. Roi
Answer: c
Solution: In the double-entry principle, we debit income and credit expenses.

The rent account will be debited with the sum of ₦50,000 in regards to the landlord (because money has been paid in as rent, e.i income), while the bank column will be credited with N50,000 (money has gone out of Mr. Rio bank account via the cheque that was issued to the landlord)

Q: Based on the Receipts and Payment Account extract showing: balance brought forward ₦3,650, subscription ₦7,500 less ₦2,000 equals ₦1,000, fees ₦8,500, insurance ₦900, rate ₦11,700, and balance carried down ₦8,050, with totals of ₦20,650 on both sides, and given the following additional information as at 1st January 1999 and 31st December 1999 respectively: rates owing ₦3,600 and ₦2,000, insurance prepaid ₦50 and ₦1,000, subscription in arrears ₦700 and ₦600, The figure ₦1000 represent What is the opening cash balance
A) ₦20,600
B) ₦8,050
C)  ₦3,650
D) ₦8,500
Answer: c
Solution: This is shown as "Bal b/f" (Balance brought forward) of ₦3,650 on the receipts side of the Receipts and Payment Account, which represents the cash balance at the beginning of the period.

Q: Shares that are offered to existing shareholders at a price is called
A) par
B) premium
C)  right issue
D) bonus issue
Answer: c
Solution: Right issue are offered to existing shareholders in a company.

Q: On 31 July 2017, Mr. Ojo provides the following information for his business:

Opening stock: ₦7,000

Closing stock: ₦12,000

Purchases: ₦60,000

Expenses: ₦4,500

Uniform gross margin: 33⅓%

Calculate the total sales for the period.
A)  ₦55,000
B) ₦82,500
C) ₦27,500
D) ₦50,000
Answer: b
Solution: COGS = Opening Stock + Purchases − Closing Stock
= 7,000 + 60,000 − 12,000 = ₦55,000

Let Sales = S
Gross margin is 33⅓%, meaning Gross Profit = 1/3 of Sales = S/3

Since:
Sales = COGS + Gross Profit
S = 55,000 + S/3

Multiply both sides by 3 to eliminate the fraction:
3S = 165,000 + S

Subtract S from both sides:
2S = 165,000

Divide both sides by 2:
S = ₦82,500

Final Answer: ₦82,500

Q: The cost of a machine is ₦10,000. The residual value is ₦4,000. It is expected to last for 4 years. Using the straight line method, what is the amount of depreciation charged per annum?
A) 6000
B) 1000
C) 1500
D) 2500
Answer: c
Solution: The formula to be adopted is :
(cost - estimated value)/(years of useful life)

(10,000 - 4000)/4 = 1500

Q: Every economic unit, regardless of its legal form of existence, is treated as a separate entity from parties having economic interest is
A) realisation concept
B) entity concept
C) going concern concept
D) matching concept
Answer: b
Solution: The entity concept ensures that only the expenses incurred by/for the business, incomes earned by the business, assets acquired for the business and liabilities owed by the business are respectively recorded as expenses, incomes, assets and liabilities in the books of the business.

Q: If only wages is shown on the trial balance, it should be charged to the
A) profit and loss account
B) trading account
C) balance sheet
D) wages account
Answer: a
Solution: Wages should be charged in the trading account only if shown separately on the trial balance from salaries. In such circumstances, the assumption, unless you are otherwise told, is that the wage is a direct trading expense to be included in the trading account while salary is an Indirect (i.e overhead) expense to be included in the P & L account.

Q: A company has two departments with the following information: opening stock for Department A is ₦100 and Department B is ₦800; purchases for Department A is ₦1,500 and Department B is ₦2,000; wages of workers is ₦50 and salaries is ₦100; sales for Department A is ₦3,000 and Department B is ₦5,000. Expenses are to be shared in the ratio of sales. The net profit for departmental A is?
A) ₦1 343.75
B) ₦1,880
C) ₦1,600
D) ₦880
Answer: a
Solution: Net profit for Department A = Sales – (Opening Stock + Purchases + Allocated Expenses)
= ₦3 000 – (₦100 + ₦1 500 + [₦150×3 000/8 000])
= ₦3 000 – (₦100 + ₦1 500 + ₦56.25)
= ₦3 000 – ₦1 656.25
= ₦1 343.75

Q: Accounting standards are issued at the International level by the
A)  Standards Advisory Council
B)  International Accounting Standards Board
C) Nigerian Accounting Standards Board
D) Standing Interpretations Committee
Answer: b
Solution: Accounting standard is a statement issued by the appropriate standard - setting body locally or internationally on a specific area or topic in Financial Accounting.
Accounting standards are issued at the International level by the International Accounting Standards Board (IASB) - formerly International Accounting Standards Committee (IASC).

Q: One of these is not a similarity between Joint Venture and Partnership.
A) AIM is profit making
B) It is for a specific venture
C) Involves two people
D) have rights and duties
Answer: b
Solution: Joint venture is for a specific venture while partnership is for a perpetual succession.

Q: Where there is no agreement made by the partners, the following provisions takes place except
A) No salary for partners acting in the business
B) There is interest on capital
C)  No interest to be charged on drawings
D) Profit and loss are to be shared equally
Answer: b
Solution: According to section 24 of the partnership Act 1890. If no specific agreement is made by the partners, the following takes place:
1. No partners may introduce a new person without the consent of all other partners 2.5% interest a year on loans made by partner e.t.c

Q: Given the following manufacturing information: stock of finished goods on January 1st was ₦50,640 and on December 31st was ₦71,380; stock of raw materials on January 1st was ₦32,160 and on December 31st was ₦29,640; purchase of raw materials was ₦145,000; manufacturing wages were ₦52,000; depreciation on factory equipment was ₦16,500; direct expenses were ₦12,500; factory fuel cost ₦7,000; and carriage inwards on raw materials was ₦7,000, what is the cost of raw materials consumed?
A) ₦154,520.
B) ₦53,000
C) ₦150,000
D) ₦152,120
Answer: a
Solution: To calculate the cost of raw materials consumed, use the formula:
Cost of Raw Materials Consumed = Opening Stock of Raw Materials + Purchases + Carriage Inwards - Closing Stock of Raw Materials
Calculation:
Cost of Raw Materials Consumed = ₦32,160 + ₦145,000 + ₦7,000 - ₦29,640
Cost of Raw Materials Consumed = ₦184,160 - ₦29,640 = ₦154,520
Therefore, the cost of raw materials consumed is ₦154,520.

Q: Using the following information: opening stock ₦20,000, purchases ₦70,000, sales ₦100,000, and closing stocks ₦15,000, what was the gross profit?
A)  ₦25,000
B) ₦35,000
C) ₦50,000
D) ₦75,000
Answer: d
Solution: To calculate the cost of goods sold, use the formula:
Cost of Goods Sold = Opening Stock + Purchases - Closing Stock
Cost of Goods Sold = ₦20,000 + ₦70,000 - ₦15,000 = ₦75,000
Therefore, the cost of goods sold was ₦75,000.

Q: A rent of ₦50,000 was paid by samson to his landlady by cheque. The double entry in Samson's book is

A)  Debit rent account, Credit bank account
B) Debit Rent account, Credit Samson's account
C) Debit Bank account, Credit Rent account
D) Debit Samson's account, Credit Rent account
Answer: b
Solution: Since Rent is receiving then rent account is debited while Samson's account is credited because it is giving out.

papers.sourceText: Q: Which of the following is not a book of original entry? A) Cash book B) Purchases journal C) Sales journal D) Ledger Answer: d Q: Use the information below to answer questions 26 and 27 Materials consumed...................₦16,600 Direct cost..........................₦5,400 Factory rent.........................₦2,300 Factory lighting.....................₦1,200 Cost of production to be transferred at cost plus 20% mark-up. The gross profit on manufacture is? A) ₦6,120 B) ₦6,100 C) ₦5,100 D) ₦5,000 Answer: c Solution: Step 1: Calculate Total Production Cost Total Production Cost = Materials consumed + Direct cost + Factory rent + Factory lighting Total Production Cost = ₦16,600 + ₦5,400 + ₦2,300 + ₦1,200 Total Production Cost = ₦25,500 Step 2: Calculate Transfer Price (Cost plus 20% mark-up) Transfer Price = Total Production Cost + (20% × Total Production Cost) Transfer Price = ₦25,500 + (0.20 × ₦25,500) Transfer Price = ₦25,500 + ₦5,100 Transfer Price = ₦30,600 Step 3: Calculate Gross Profit on Manufacture Gross Profit on Manufacture = Transfer Price - Total Production Cost Gross Profit on Manufacture = ₦30,600 - ₦25,500 Gross Profit on Manufacture = ₦5,100 Q: Asa Company bought a vehicle worth ₦20,000 and the vehicle is to be depreciated at 5%. Using the reducing balance method of depreciation, what would be the value of the asset after 3 years? A) ₦19,000.00 B) ₦18,050.50 C) ₦17,147.50 D) 16,290.13 Answer: c Solution: To find the value of the asset after 3 years using the reducing balance method, Apply the 5% depreciation rate to the remaining balance each year. Given information: Original cost: ₦20,000 Depreciation rate: 5% per annum Method: Reducing balance Period: 3 years Year-by-year calculation: Year 1: Depreciation = ₦20,000 × 5% = ₦1,000 Book value = ₦20,000 - ₦1,000 = ₦19,000 Year 2: Depreciation = ₦19,000 × 5% = ₦950 Book value = ₦19,000 - ₦950 = ₦18,050 Year 3: Depreciation = ₦18,050 × 5% = ₦902.50 Book value = ₦18,050 - ₦902.50 = ₦17,147.50 Alternative formula method: Book value = Original cost × (1 - depreciation rate)^number of years Book value = ₦20,000 × (1 - 0.05)³ Book value = ₦20,000 × (0.95)³ Book value = ₦20,000 × 0.857375 Book value = ₦17,147.50 Q: Given: Capital ...........₦1000 Liabilities........₦500 Assets.............₦1500 The accounting equation can be expressed as? A) ₦1000 + ₦500 + ₦1500 = ₦3000 B) ₦1000 - ₦500 + ₦1500 = ₦2000 C) ₦1000 + ₦500 = ₦1500 D) ₦1500 + ₦500 = ₦2000 Answer: c Solution: The fundamental accounting equation is: Assets = Capital + Liabilities Given: Capital = ₦1,000 Liabilities = ₦500 Assets = ₦1,500 Substituting into the equation: ₦1,500 = ₦1,000 + ₦500 ₦1,500 = ₦1,500 Q: Statement of assets and liabilities as at 31st December, 2001. Shareholders' interest ₦240 Current liabilities ₦20 Current assets ₦110 Fixed assets ₦140 What is the networking capital? A) ₦90 B) ₦70 C) ₦100 D) ₦80 Answer: a Solution: Working capital (also called net working capital) is calculated as Current Assets minus Current Liabilities. Working Capital = Current Assets - Current Liabilities Working Capital = ₦110 - ₦20 = ₦90 The working capital is ₦90. Q: Which of the following is not a feature of accounting information? A) Affordability B) Timeliness C) Accuracy D) Completeness Answer: a Q: In the public sector, the method of accounting that reports revenues and expenditures in the period in which they are received and paid is called? A) fund accounting B) commitment accounting C) cash accounting D) accrual accounting Answer: c Solution: Reason: In public sector cash accounting, revenue is recorded when received and expenditure when paid, without regard to the period the transactions actually relate to. Q: The power to appoint the Auditor General of the Federation is vested in the A) National Assembly B) Civil Service Commission C) Judicial Service Commission D) President Answer: d Solution: In Nigeria, the power to appoint the Auditor General of the Federation is vested in the President. This appointment is made subject to confirmation by the Senate, as provided for in the Nigerian Constitution. Q: The trading account is to a sole trader what income and expenditure account is to a? A) partnership B) public limited organization C) manufacturing organization D) non-profit making organization Answer: d Solution: The trading account is to a sole trader what the income and expenditure account is to a non-profit making organization. Q: If a sole proprietorship is purchased for cash, then? A) the purchaser debits his business purchase account with the consideration he pays B) all assets and liabilities must be bought C) goodwill results where value of assets D) the vendor debits his business purchase account with the considerstion he receives Answer: a Solution: The purchaser records the total purchase price in a "Business Purchase Account" or similar account, which is then analyzed and allocated to individual assets and goodwill. Q: The costs of acquiring fixed assets and bringing them into the firm is a A) general expenses B) recurrent expenditure C) revenue expenditure D) capital expenditure. Answer: d Q: The double entry to record the proceeds on disposal of assets is debit A) Bank Account; credit Asset Disposal Account. B) Asset Disposal Account; credit Bank Account. C) Provision for Depreciation Account; credit Asset Disposal Account D) Asset Disposal Account; credit Provision for Depreciation Account. Answer: a Q: Which of the following demonstrates the imprest system? A) Float → expenses paid → cash in bank → float B) Float → cash from bank → expenses paid → float C) Float → expenses paid→ cash from bank → float D) Float → cash in bank → expenses paid → float Answer: c Solution: Under the imprest system, you start with a fixed petty cash float. As expenses are paid out of that float, its balance declines. At the end of the period (or when replenishment is needed), you draw cash from the bank equal to the total expenses paid to restore the float back to its original amount. Q: A pension granted to any past president or vice-president shall be charged to the A) consolidated revenue fund B) special pension fund C) contingency fund D) development fund. Answer: b Q: A complete set of financial statements for Hartman Company, at December 31, 1999, would include each of the following except: A) Balance sheet as of December 31,1999 B) Income statement for the year ended December 31, 1999. C) Statement of projected cash flows for 2000 D) Notes containing additional information that is useful interpreting the financial statements. Answer: c Q: A business has the following information for a trading period: Stock Jan 1 ₦2600, Purchases ₦4000, Carriage inwards ₦500, Sales ₦9000, Carriage outwards ₦500. Determine the net profit. A) ₦4,000 B) ₦4,500 C) . ₦5,000 D) ₦1,400 Answer: d Solution: Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases + Carriage inwards = ₦2,600 + ₦4,000 + ₦500 = ₦7,100 Gross profit = Sales − Cost of goods sold = ₦9,000 − ₦7,100 = ₦1,900 Net profit = Gross profit − Carriage outwards = ₦1,900 − ₦500 = ₦1,400. Q: Use the information below to answer questions 27 to 28 Purchase:..Raw materials.................₦15 000 Finished goods...........................₦11 400 Stock:....(1/7/01)Raw materials..........₦2 250 Work-in-progress.........................₦1 875 Wages:.....Direct........................₦17 100 Indirect.................................₦5 400 Stock:.....(30/06/02)Raw materials.......₦3 000 Work-in-progress.........................₦3 375 The cost of raw materials consumed is? A) ₦17 250 B) ₦15 750 C) ₦15 000 D) ₦14 250 Answer: d Solution: Opening raw materials = ₦2,250 Add: Purchases of raw materials = ₦15,000 Less: Closing raw materials = ₦3,000 Raw materials consumed = 2,250 + 15,000 − 3,000 = ₦14,250 Q: The principle of double entry developed from the axioms of accounting equation is given as A) Liabilties + Equity = Net assets B) Assets + Equity = Liabilities C) Liabilities + Equity = Assets D) Assets + Liability = Equity Answer: c Solution: The accounting equation states that: - Capital( Equity) = Assets - Liabilities - Assets = Capital (Equity) - Liabilties - Liabilties = Assets - Capital (Equity) - Equity(Capital ) = Assets Q: In a three-column cash book, the discount allowed is shown on the? A) debit side B) credit side C) folio column D) memorandum column Answer: a Solution: Discount allowed is an expense (a reduction in cash received), so it’s recorded on the debit side of the three-column cash book. (By contrast, discount received is shown on the credit side.) Q: One of the items listed below will not be found in a company’s memorandum and article of association. Which is it? A) objects and their alteration B) location of business C) bank signatories D) powers of directors Answer: c Solution: Bank signatories will not be found in a company's memorandum and articles of association because: Bank signatories are operational details determined by the board of directors They are recorded in board resolutions and banking mandates, not in the constitutional documents These details can change frequently and don't require constitutional amendments Q: Which of the following are advantages of departmental accounts? A) the capital of the business can be calculated easily B) easy knowledge of the sources of funding C) encouragement of healthy rivalry among the various department D) the department making the highest profit can be easily determined Answer: c Solution: Departmental accounts help create healthy competition between departments by making each department's performance visible and comparable. This motivates department managers to improve efficiency and profitability. Q: From Zahki Plc's balance sheet as at 31st December 1997, the company has the following financial position: On the equity and liabilities side - Paid up capital of ₦200,000, Share premium of ₦15,000, Profit and loss account balance of ₦60,000, Long-term loan of ₦180,000, Creditors of ₦200,000, and Other current liabilities of ₦100,000, totaling ₦755,000. On the assets side - Fixed assets of ₦300,000, Investment of ₦180,000, Stock of ₦28,000, Debtors of ₦90,000 with a provision of ₦3,000 making net debtors ₦87,000, Cash of ₦60,000, and Bank of ₦100,000, also totaling ₦755,000. What is the quick ratio? A) 0.82 : 1 B) 1:53:01 C) 0.95:1 D) 0.91:1 Answer: a Solution: Quick Ratio (Acid‐Test Ratio) is calculated as: (Current Assets − Stock)/Current Liabilities ​ Current Assets (excluding stock): Net Debtors ₦87,000 + Cash ₦60,000 + Bank ₦100,000 = ₦247,000 Current Liabilities: Creditors ₦200,000 + Other Current Liabilities ₦100,000 = ₦300,000 Quick Ratio: 247,000/300,000 ≈ 0.82:1 So the quick ratio is 0.82 : 1. Q: Given: I. Cash refunds II. Debit note issued III. Dishnoured cheque IV. Purchases The item on the credit side of purchase ledger control account includes A) I, II and IV only B) I and IV only C) I and II only D) I, II and III only Answer: b Solution: The item on the credit side of the purchase control account or total creditor control account are: purchase (credit), cash refunds, discount withdrawn, debit note received. Q: Use the information below to answer questions 41 and 42 Given the following information: Authorized capital of ₦100,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each, issued and fully paid 50,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each amounting to ₦50,000, 10,000 8% preference shares of ₦1 each, reserves ₦10,000, creditors ₦25,000, debtors ₦13,000, and cash in hand ₦5,000. Calculate the shareholder’sfund. A) ₦70,000. B) ₦75,000 C) ₦85,000 D) ₦185,000 Answer: a Solution: Shareholders' fund represents the total equity belonging to shareholders, which includes share capital and reserves. Shareholders' Fund consists of: Ordinary share capital (issued and fully paid): ₦50,000 8% preference shares: ₦10,000 Reserves: ₦10,000 Total Shareholders' Fund = ₦50,000 + ₦10,000 + ₦10,000 = ₦70,000 Therefore, the shareholders' fund is ₦70,000. Q: When a purchase business is revalued, the effect is that? A) a decrease in the value of asset has no effect on value of goodwill B) an increase in the value of asset is treated as an increase in the value of goodwill C) a decrease in the value of asset is treated as an decrease in the value of goodwil D) an increase in the value of asset is treated as an decrease in the value of goodwill Answer: d Solution: When you revalue the acquired business’s assets upward, the net asset base increases, and since Goodwill is calculated as: Goodwill = Purchase Consideration − Fair Value of Net Assets an increase in asset values will reduce the calculated Goodwill. Q: When forming a partnership, new partners should record non-monetary assets on the new partnership's books at? A) their current fair market values B) their historical costs when first use C) their historical costs when first purchase by each new partner D) the highest values practical so that future income tax deductions are maximized Answer: a Solution: Non-monetary assets contributed by new partners must be brought into the partnership at their current fair market values as of the date of contribution, to ensure that capital accounts accurately reflect the economic value each partner has invested. Q: The difference between double entry and single entry is A) double entry is based on the dual concept while single entry is not based on dual concept B) double entry is an account while single entry is not an account C) double entry keeps personal account while single does not D) double entry is useful for business enterprise while single entry is not Answer: a Solution: Double entry is based on dual concept, i.e two-fold aspect of transaction whereby single entry ignored the principle of double entry. Q: Use the information below to answer questions 14 and 15 Palaju Enterprises had fixed assets of ₦3,100,000 at the end of the year. Fixed assets costing ₦900,000 with provision for depreciation of ₦150,000 were disposed of during the period. Fixed assets of ₦100,000 were added during the year. Provision for depreciation was ₦350,000 at the beginning of the year and ₦300,000 at the end of the year. What was the value of fixed assets at the beginning of the year? A) ₦2,900,000 B) ₦3,800,000 C) ₦3,900,000 D) ₦4,000,000 Answer: c Solution: Opening Balance + Additions - Disposals = Closing Balance Rearranging to find Opening Balance: Opening Balance = Closing Balance + Disposals - Additions Substituting the values: Opening Balance = ₦3,100,000 + ₦900,000 - ₦100,000 Opening Balance = ₦4,000,000 - ₦100,000 = ₦3,900,000 Q: Using the given information, calculate the acid test ratio: Stock: ₦11,250 Debtors: ₦18,750 Creditors: ₦3,750 Bank: ₦4,000 Net profit: ₦7,500 Net: ₦60,000 A) 5 : 1 B) 6 : 1 C) 6 : 1 : 1 D) 4 : 1 Answer: b Solution: Quick assets = Debtors + Bank = 18,750 + 4,000 = 22,750 Acid-test ratio = Quick assets/Creditors = 22,750/3,750 ≈ 6.06 : 1. Rounded to the nearest whole‐number ratio, that’s 6 : 1. Q: Bank reconciliation statement reconciles A) bank and cash balances in the cash book B) bank balance in the cash book and bank statement balance C) cash balance in the cash book and bank statement balance D) bank balance brought down and bank balance carried down in the cash bcok. Answer: b Q: In a departmental accounting system, which of the following expenses will most likely be apportioned on the basis of turnover A) carriage inwards B) carriage outwards C) discount received D) returns outwards Answer: b Solution: Carriage outwards (distribution or delivery expense) varies directly with sales activity and is therefore apportioned to departments based on their relative turnover. Carriage inwards relates to purchases, while discount received and returns outwards aren’t selling‐related expenses. Q: An advantage of control account is A) locating figures. B) adding figures. C) changing figures. D) locating errors. Answer: d Q: The amount to be charged to the profit and loss account is A) N 30,000 B) N25,000 C) N 5 ,000 D) N20,000. Answer: b Q: Which of the following methods gives a conservative closing stock value during a period of rising prices? A) LIFO B) FIFO C) Simple average D) Periodic simple average Answer: a Q: Which of the following is the equation for determining net profit or loss from the records of a firm? A) Closing Capital - Drawings - Capital Introduced B) Opening Capital + Drawings - Closing Capital C) Closing Capital + Opening Capital - Drawings D) Closing Capital + Drawings - Opening Capital Answer: d Q: Mr Bassey purchased a motor vehicle for use in his business and debited the purchases account with the same value. This is an error of? A) omission B) principle C) commission D) original entry Answer: b Solution: Explanation: An error of principle occurs when a transaction is recorded in the wrong type of account, here, a capital expenditure (motor vehicle) was recorded as revenue expenditure (purchases). Q: The main objective of accounting report is to provide information about? A) a company's shareholding B) an entity's management C) the efficacy of assets D) a company's economic resources Answer: d Solution: The primary purpose of an accounting report is to convey information about an entity’s economic resources (its assets) and the claims against those resources, as well as changes in them over time. Q: Where the debit side of the income and expenditure account is higher than the credit side, the difference is A) deficit B) surplus C) gain D) loss Answer: a Q: The recording phase of accounting is known as? A) bookkeeping B) trial balancing C) ledger accounting D) final accounting Answer: a Solution: Reason: bookkeeping is the stage where transactions are recorded (journals, ledgers, subsidiary books). Trial balancing, ledger accounting and final accounting are later stages. Q: Processed data is only useful to user if it is A) complex B) quantitative C) relevant D) qualitative Answer: c Solution: first thing to be considered when gathering data is the relevant and usefulness of the data or information before considering the qualitative aspect and other things Relevant : even if the information of data is not processed, if the processed data is relevant, it will be useful to the user

Q: Fiyinfoluwa Motors bought three Toyota Hilux vans on cash at the cost of ₦6,000,000 on debiting the vehicle account, the corresponding credit for the purchase will appear in the
A) sales day book
B) cash book
C)  sales subsidiary book
D) purchase day book
Answer: b
Solution: Since the vans were purchased for cash, the corresponding credit entry is made in the cash book (which records all cash payments), not in any of the sales or purchase day books (which are used for credit transactions).

Q: The major feature of a journal is that it has
A) five columns, date, particulars, folio, debit and credit
B) three columns, date, particulars, folio and amount
C) Six columns, date. particulars, folio, amount debit and credit
D)  four columns, date, particulars, folio and amount
Answer: a
Solution: A typical journal entry usually has four columns: the date of the transaction, the particulars, and columns for the debits and credits.

Sometimes, the folio column can be included, but is it not a compulsory requirement.

Q: Use the information below to answer this question

A machine bought for ₦35,000 was estimated to have a life span of 5 years with a scrap value of ₦9000.
 

The yearly depreciation using the straight-line method would be

A) ₦5200
B) ₦800
C) ₦6500
D) ₦4400
Answer: a
Solution: COGS = Cost – Scrap Value = 35,000 – 9,000 = ₦26,000
Annual Depreciation = COGS ÷ Useful Life = 26,000 ÷ 5 = ₦5,200

Q: Four broad classifications of overheads are
A) production, selling, distribution and administration
B) production, selling, distribution and material
C) selling, distribution and material
D)  distribution, selling, administration and materials
Answer: a
Solution: These are the four standard classifications of overheads in cost accounting:

Production - factory-related indirect costs
Selling - costs to promote and secure sales
Distribution - costs to deliver goods to customers
Administration - general management and office expenses

Material is not an overhead classification since materials are typically direct costs, not indirect overheads.

Q: A company has departments L, M and O. Department L Occupies a space twice that of M while O occupies half the space of M. If the company pays ₦70,000 on rent, what is the amount of rent that should be allocated to M?
A)  ₦40,000
B) ₦20,000
C)  ₦30,000
D) ₦10,000
Answer: b
Solution: Step 1: Determine the space ratios

Let M's space = 1 unit
L's space = 2 units (twice that of M)
O's space = 0.5 units (half that of M)
Total space = 2 + 1 + 0.5 = 3.5 units

Step 2: Calculate M's proportion

M's proportion = 1 ÷ 3.5 = 2/7

Step 3: Allocate rent to M

M's rent allocation = 2/7 × ₦70,000 = ₦20,000

Q: The standing order is a payment instruction given by a
A) customer to a fellow customer
B) bank to an employee
C) customer to the bank
D) bank to the customers
Answer: c
Solution: A standing order is a payment instruction given by a customer to their bank to make regular fixed payments to a specified recipient on predetermined dates. The customer authorizes the bank to automatically transfer a fixed amount from their account at regular intervals (monthly, quarterly, etc.) without requiring further authorization for each payment.

Q: Danjuma Ltd. bought 10 bags of rice for N500 each. The company was given 5% and 12% trade and cash discounts respectively. What will be recorded as discount received in the company's book?
A) ₦250
B) ₦570
C)  ₦850
D)  ₦600
Answer: b
Solution: 
Trade discount (5%) reduces the list cost and isn’t separately recorded in the books:

10 × ₦500 = ₦5,000 ⟹ ₦5,000 × 5% = ₦250
Net after trade discount = ₦5,000 − ₦250 = ₦4,750.

Cash discount (12%) is the one actually recorded as “Discount Received”:

₦4,750 × 12% = ₦570.
Hence, the company will record ₦570 as discount received.

Q: Which of the following accounting records are source documents?
A)  journals and ledgers
B) sales invoice and debit note
C) sales invoice and cashbook
D)  cashbook and debit note
Answer: b
Solution: Source documents are the original vouchers evidencing that a transaction has occurred. A sales invoice and a debit note are both such vouchers. In contrast, journals, ledgers, and the cashbook are accounting records prepared from those source documents.

Q: The debenture issued at price  above the nominal value is Said to be issued at a
A) margin
B) premium
C) cost price
D) mark-up
Answer: b
Solution: When a debenture is issued at a price above its nominal (face) value, it is said to be issued at a premium. For example, if a debenture with a nominal value of ₦100 is issued for ₦110, it is issued at a premium of ₦10.

Q: In preparing accounting records, the owners of a business and the business are treated as
A) separate legal entities
B) partners
C) the same person
D) having business relationship
Answer: a
Solution: Under the business entity (or separate entity) concept, the affairs of the owners and those of the business are kept completely distinct. Personal transactions of the owners are not recorded in the business’s books, and only business‑related transactions appear in the accounting records.

Q: Using the information provided: capital opening balance ₦307,000, closing balance ₦342,000, net profit for the period ₦121,600, purchases ₦706,000, carriage inwards ₦17,500, cost of goods sold ₦740,700, total selling, general and administration expenses ₦526,000, discount received ₦9,650, and opening stock ₦98,800, What is the gross profit for the period?
A) ₦637,950
B) ₦628,300
C)  ₦647,600
D) ₦106,400
Answer: a
Solution: To find the gross profit, first calculate sales from the given information, then subtract cost of goods sold.
From the profit and loss relationship:
Net Profit = Gross Profit - Operating Expenses + Other Income
₦121,600 = Gross Profit - ₦526,000 + ₦9,650
Rearranging:
Gross Profit = ₦121,600 + ₦526,000 - ₦9,650 = ₦637,950
Alternatively, using the gross profit formula:
Sales = Cost of Goods Sold + Gross Profit
Sales = ₦740,700 + Gross Profit
From the net profit calculation:
Sales - ₦740,700 - ₦526,000 + ₦9,650 = ₦121,600
Sales = ₦1,378,650
Therefore: Gross Profit = ₦1,378,650 - ₦740,700 = ₦637,950
The gross profit for the period is ₦637,950.RetryClaude can make mistakes. Please double-check responses. Sonnet 4

Q: Which of the following are advantages of departmental accounts?
A)  the capital of the business can be calculated easily
B) easy knowledge of the sources of funding
C) encouragement of healthy rivalry among the various department
D) the department making the highest profit can be easily determined
Answer: c
Solution: Departmental accounts help create healthy competition between departments by making each department's performance visible and comparable. This motivates department managers to improve efficiency and profitability.

Q: One of the major features of book keeping is that it
A) is futuristic in nature
B) accepts responsibility for all wrong postings
C) provides permanent records for all financial transactions
D) does not give room for double entry procedure
Answer: c
Solution: One of the core purposes of bookkeeping is to systematically record and maintain an ongoing, permanent record of every financial transaction of the business. This ensures accuracy, auditability, and continuity in the accounting process.

Q: Which of the following accounting conventions suggests that accountants should use a method of valuation that understates rather than overstates results?
A) monetary
B) cost
C) conservatism
D) historical
Answer: c
Solution: The conservatism convention (also known as prudence) suggests that accountants should use methods of valuation that understate rather than overstate results

Q: Accrual accounting differs from cash accounting because it recognizes
A) prepayment and cash
B) cash and creditors
C) cash and debtors
D)  debtors and creditors
Answer: d
Solution: Accrual accounting differs from cash accounting because it records transactions when they occur, regardless of when cash is received or paid. This means it recognizes:

Debtors (amounts owed to the business) - revenue earned but not yet received in cash
Creditors (amounts owed by the business) - expenses incurred but not yet paid in cash

Cash accounting only records transactions when cash actually changes hands, while accrual accounting recognizes these outstanding amounts (debtors and creditors) that represent future cash flows.

Q: Which of the following errors will affect the trial balance total?
A) omission of sales of ₦3000 and purchases of ₦2000
B)  Posting discount allowed to the debit side of discount allowed account
C)  omission of one account from the list when extracting the ledgers
D) failure to post sales of ₦2000 and purchases of ₦2000
Answer: a
Solution:  Omission of sales of ₦3,000 and purchases of ₦2,000:

Sales (credit) ₦3,000 missing and purchases (debit) ₦2,000 missing
Net effect: Credit side short by ₦1,000
This affects the trial balance total

Q: The power to appoint the Auditor General of the Federation is vested in the
A) National Assembly
B) Civil Service Commission
C)  Judicial Service Commission
D) President
Answer: d
Solution: In Nigeria, the power to appoint the Auditor General of the Federation is vested in the President. This appointment is made subject to confirmation by the Senate, as provided for in the Nigerian Constitution.

Q: Advertising expenses incurred on a product in a business organization should be charged to
A) production department
B) purchases department
C) sales department
D) administrative department
Answer: c
Solution: Advertising is a selling expense aimed at promoting products and generating sales. In departmental accounting, such costs are allocated to the sales department since they directly support the selling function rather than production, purchasing, or general administration.

Q: Given the following information: stock on 1/4/94 was ₦800, purchases of flour ₦2,450, sales ₦4,745, wages of bakery staff ₦675, carriage outwards ₦50, salary of administrative staff ₦22, stock on 31/3/95 was ₦940, and capital ₦1,540, calculate the cost of goods sold.
A)  ₦3,925
B)  ₦3,250
C)  ₦2,985
D) ₦2,575
Answer: c
Solution: From the given information:

Opening Stock (1/4/94) = ₦800
Purchases of flour = ₦2,450
Wages of bakery staff (direct labor) = ₦675
Closing Stock (31/3/95) = ₦940

Cost of Goods Sold = ₦800 + ₦2,450 + ₦675 - ₦940
Cost of Goods Sold = ₦3,925 - ₦940 = ₦2,985
Therefore, the cost of goods sold is ₦2,985.

Q: The addition of prime cost, indirect cost and opening work- in-progress less the closing work-in-progress will result in cost of
A) goods manufactured
B) materials put into production
C)  goods available for sale
D) goods sold
Answer: a
Solution: The formula given represents the calculation for cost of goods manufactured:
Cost of Goods Manufactured = Prime Cost + Indirect Cost + Opening Work-in-Progress - Closing Work-in-Progress

Q: Given the following information from the Appropriation Account showing distributions to partners TAYO and TOPE: Interest on capital amounts to ₦750 for TAYO and ₦550 for TOPE; Salaries are ₦800 for TAYO and ₦600 for TOPE; Share of profit is ₦3,300 for TAYO and ₦3,300 for TOPE. You are required to determine the net profits of the partnership.
A) ₦6,600
B) ₦9,300
C) ₦4,450
D)  ₦4,850
Answer: b
Solution: The net profit of the partnership is the total of all appropriations:

Interest on capital: ₦750 + ₦550 = ₦1,300

Salaries: ₦800 + ₦600 = ₦1,400

Partners’ profit share: ₦3,300 + ₦3,300 = ₦6,600

So

Net Profit=1,300+1,400+6,600= 
₦9,300

Q: The term "accounting period" is used to refer to the
A) time span, usually one year covered by the financial statement
B) period within which debtors are expected to settle accounts
C)  time, span during which taxes are paid to the inland revenue board
D)  budget period, usually one year relied on by the accountant
Answer: a
Solution: The accounting period concept divides a business’s life into regular, comparable intervals—most commonly one year—for which financial statements are prepared. This allows stakeholders to assess performance and financial position over consistent time spans

Q: ₦500 monthly is allowed on an imprest system. The following transactions took place in Period 1: cash advanced to petty cashier ₦500, petty cashier paid out for stamp ₦200 and newspaper ₦250. In Period 2: cash to petty cashier ₦450, cashier paid for writing materials ₦350. How much should the petty cashier receive after period 2?
A)  ₦150
B)  ₦350
C) ₦250
D)  ₦500
Answer: b
Solution: After Period 2:

Opening balance: ₦50 + Cash received ₦450 = ₦500
Payment made: Writing materials ₦350
Balance remaining: ₦500 - ₦350 = ₦150

To restore the imprest to ₦500:
Amount needed = ₦500 - ₦150 = ₦350
Therefore, the petty cashier should receive ₦350 after period 2.

Q: In trial balance, income and liabilities are
A) credited
B) credited and debited respectively
C) debited and credited respectively
D) debited
Answer: a
Solution: In a trial balance, both income and liabilities appear on the credit side. This follows the fundamental accounting principle:

Income/Revenue accounts have credit balances because they increase owner's equity
Liability accounts have credit balances because they represent amounts owed by the business

Q: The rule of accounting equation requires that account payable should be placed under
A) equities
B) assets
C) capital
D) liabilities
Answer: d
Solution: Accounts payable represent amounts the business owes to suppliers and are therefore classified as liabilities in the accounting equation (Assets = Liabilities + Equity).

Q: Using the information provided: capital opening balance ₦307,000, closing balance ₦342,000, net profit for the period ₦121,600, purchases ₦706,000, carriage inwards ₦17,500, cost of goods sold ₦740,700, total selling, general and administration expenses ₦526,000, discount received ₦9,650, and opening stock ₦98,800, calculate the closing stock for the period.
A) ₦69,300
B) ₦81,600
C)  ₦81,300
D) ₦106,400
Answer: b
Solution: To calculate closing stock, use the cost of goods sold formula and rearrange:
Cost of Goods Sold = Opening Stock + Purchases + Carriage Inwards - Closing Stock
Rearranging to find closing stock:
Closing Stock = Opening Stock + Purchases + Carriage Inwards - Cost of Goods Sold
Closing Stock = ₦98,800 + ₦706,000 + ₦17,500 - ₦740,700
Closing Stock = ₦822,300 - ₦740,700 = ₦81,600
Therefore, the closing stock for the period is ₦81,600.

Q: Given the following list of balances: bank account ₦59,410, capital account ₦50,000, purchases account ₦20,000, rent ₦2,500, stationery ₦90, typewriter ₦6,500, and sales ₦38,500, in preparing a trial balance from this list of balances, what is the total in debit and credit columns?
A)  ₦I38,500
B)  ₦147,910
C) ₦85,800
D)  ₦88,500
Answer: d
Solution: Debits: Bank ₦59,410 + Purchases ₦20,000 + Rent ₦2,500 + Stationery ₦90 + Typewriter ₦6,500 = ₦88,500

Credits: Capital ₦50,000 + Sales ₦38,500 = ₦88,500

Q: Using the information provided: total current assets ₦2,000, total fixed assets ₦4,000, current liabilities ₦1,200, drawings ₦200, and long term loan ₦2,000, What is the net working capital?
A)  ₦1,800
B) ₦800
C)  ₦2,600
D)  ₦600
Answer: b
Solution: Current Assets−Current Liabilities=₦2,000−₦1,200=₦800

Q: In a control account, provision for bad debts is found on the
A) credit side of the sales ledger control account
B) debit side of the purchases ledger control açcount
C) debit side of the sales ledger control account
D)  credit side of the purchases ledger control account
Answer: a
Solution: The provision for bad debts reduces the net amount owed by customers, so it is recorded as a credit in the Sales Ledger Control Account to offset (reduce) the balance of debtors.

Q: Kola and Sunday are in partnership sharing profits and losses equally. If Kemi is admitted as a new partner to take 1/5 as her share, what is the new profit or loss sharing ratio?
A) Kola 1/3, Sunday 1/3 and Kemi 1/3
B) Kola 1/5, Sunday 1/5 and Kemi 3/5
C)  Kola 2/5, Sunday 1/5 and Kemi 2/5
D) Kola 2/5, Sunday 2/5 and Kemi 1/5
Answer: d
Solution: Step 1: Kemi is admitted with a 1/5 share
Step 2: The remaining share for old partners = 1 - 1/5 = 4/5
Step 3: Since Kola and Sunday were sharing equally before admission, they will continue to share the remaining 4/5 equally between themselves
New sharing ratio:

Kola: 4/5 ÷ 2 = 2/5
Sunday: 4/5 ÷ 2 = 2/5
Kemi: 1/5

Verification: 2/5 + 2/5 + 1/5 = 5/5 = 1

Q: A major cause of discrepancy between the bank statement and the cashbook that overstates the bank statement balance is the
A) commission paid
B)  interest received
C) direct withdrawal
D) direct payment
Answer: b
Solution: When the bank credits your account with interest, it appears immediately on the bank statement but isn’t yet recorded in your cashbook. This makes the bank statement balance higher than the cashbook balance until you record the interest in your books.

Q: Use the information below to answer this question

A machine bought for ₦35,000 was estimated to have a life span of 5 years with a scrap value of ₦9000.

If the scrap value is presently ₦15,000 what will be the yearly depreciation using straight-line method?
A) ₦7,000
B) ₦11,000
C) ₦4,000
D) ₦24,000
Answer: c
Solution: The annual depreciation under the straight‐line method is calculated as:

(Cost−Revised Scrap Value)/​Useful Life
 = (35000−15000)/5​
 = 20000/5
​
 =₦4000

So the yearly depreciation is ₦4,000.

Q: The amount of subscriptions accrued is reported in the balance sheet under
A) fixed cost
B) current asset
C)  long term liability
D) current liability
Answer: b
Solution: Accrued subscriptions represent amounts due from members for subscriptions earned but not yet received in cash. As such receivables are expected to be collected within the year, they are classified as a current asset on the balance sheet.

Q: In the head office ledger, the value of goods sent to the branch are
A) debited to the branch current account
B) debited to the head office current account
C)  credited to the head office current account
D) credited to the branch current account
Answer: a
Solution: In the head office’s ledger, each branch has its own current (or “branch”) account. When goods are sent from head office to a branch, the head office debited the Branch Current Account (reflecting an asset transfer to the branch) and credited the Head Office’s Inventory or Stock Account. This debit entry increases the branch’s account balance, showing the value of goods supplied.

Q: Under which of the following conditions is a partnership dissolved?
A)  change of the partnership's head office
B)  purchase of a large quantity of fixed assets
C)  admission of a new partner
D) retirement of a manager who is not a partner
Answer: c
Solution: Legally, the admission of a new partner brings about the dissolution of the existing partnership and the formation of a new one (even though the business may continue uninterrupted). None of the other events (moving the head office, buying fixed assets, or a manager’s retirement when they aren’t a partner) automatically dissolve the partnership.

Q: Five hundred naira monthly is allowed on an imprest system. The following transactions took place in Period 1: cash advanced to petty cashier ₦500, petty cashier paid out for stamp ₦200 and newspaper ₦250. In Period 2: cash to petty cashier ₦450, cashier paid for writing materials ₦350. What was the balance of cash with the petty cashier at the end of period 1?
A)  ₦450
B)  ₦300
C) ₦50
D)  ₦200
Answer: c
Solution: Under the imprest system, the petty cashier should always maintain a fixed float of ₦500.
After Period 1:

Opening balance: ₦500
Payments made: Stamp ₦200 + Newspaper ₦250 = ₦450
Balance remaining: ₦500 - ₦450 = ₦50



Q: Using the information provided: total current assets ₦2,000, total fixed assets ₦4,000, current liabilities ₦1,200, drawings ₦200, and long term loan ₦2,000, calculate the capital of the business.
A) ₦2,800.
B) ₦9,400
C)  ₦3,400
D) ₦6,000
Answer: a
Solution: To calculate capital, use the accounting equation:
Assets = Liabilities + Capital
First, calculate total assets and total liabilities:
Total Assets = Current Assets + Fixed Assets
Total Assets = ₦2,000 + ₦4,000 = ₦6,000
Total Liabilities = Current Liabilities + Long Term Loan
Total Liabilities = ₦1,200 + ₦2,000 = ₦3,200
Using the accounting equation:
Capital = Total Assets - Total Liabilities
Capital = ₦6,000 - ₦3,200 = ₦2,800
Note: Drawings represent owner's withdrawals and don't affect the capital calculation using the accounting equation method.
Therefore, the capital of the business is ₦2,800.

Q: The rules which govern the internal management of a firm and its financial affairs in a partnership business is a
A) memoransum
B) deed
C)  financial regulation
D) bye-law
Answer: b
Solution: In a partnership business, the rules governing internal management and financial affairs are contained in a partnership deed (also called a partnership agreement).

Q: The value of the sales ledger control account is derived from the summation of the
A) total creditors control account
B) total debtors control account
C) all day books
D) both the debtors and creditors accounts
Answer: b
Solution: The sales ledger control account (also known as the debtors control account) represents the total amount owed by all customers who have purchased goods on credit. Its value is derived from the summation of all individual debtor balances in the sales ledger.

Q: The major distinguishing element between the final accounts of a partnership and a sole trader is the
A) drawings account
B) appropriation account
C) capital account
D) creditors account
Answer: b
Solution: In a sole trader’s final accounts, after the Trading and Profit & Loss Account, the net profit is simply transferred to the proprietor’s capital account. A partnership, however, requires an additional Appropriation Account to show how the net profit is distributed among partners (interest on capital, salaries, profit shares, etc.). This “profit distribution” step is unique to partnerships.

papers.sourceText: Q: Which of the following entries is effected by a department when goods are charged to it at selling prices? A) stock account is debited B) purchases account is debited C) stock account is credited D) mark-up account is debited Answer: d Solution: When goods are transferred to a department at the selling price, the department must separate the cost and the markup. The markup portion is removed from the stock valuation by debiting the Mark-up Account. Q: According to the provisions of the 1999 Constitution, all revenues generated by the Federal Government must be paid into the? A) Consolidated Revenue Fund B) Federation Account C) Revenue Mobilization Allocation and Fiscal Commission's Account D) Equalization Fund Answer: a Solution: Section 80 of the 1999 Constitution requires that all revenues or other moneys raised or received by the Federation shall be paid into and form one Consolidated Revenue Fund of the Federation Q: The book value per share is obtained by dividing A) shareholders equity by outstanding shares B) total assets by outstanding shares C) gross profit by outstanding shares D) net profit by outstanding shares Answer: a Q: The trading account is to a sole trader what income and expenditure account is to a? A) partnership B) public limited organization C) manufacturing organization D) non-profit making organization Answer: d Solution: The trading account is to a sole trader what the income and expenditure account is to a non-profit making organization. Q: Which of the following is not part of the main uses of the journal A) purchase and sale of fixed assets on credit B) the correction of errors C) writing off bad debts D) none of the above Answer: d Q: Which of the following is not found in the personal ledger? A) Debtors Account B) Creditors Account C) Capital Account D) Nominal Account Answer: c Q: Goods stolen at the branch is debited to A) branch stock account B) defalcations account C) branch debtors account D) branch adjustment account Answer: b Solution: When goods are stolen at a branch, this represents a loss due to dishonest activities or theft. In accounting, such losses are recorded in a defalcations account, which is specifically used to track losses arising from fraud, theft, or other dishonest acts. Q: If a property developing company sells a completed building to an interested third party, this sale can be treated in the books of the company as? A) capital receipt B) revenue receipt C) windfall receipt D) miscellaneous receipt Answer: b Solution: For a property developing company, selling a completed building would be treated as a revenue receipt. A property developing company is in the business of constructing and selling buildings The completed building represents stock/inventory for this type of company When sold, it generates income from the company's normal business operations This is similar to how a manufacturing company treats the sale of its manufactured goods Q: Net profit in a business is A) the amount of money taken out of the business by the owner B) the cash in the business bank account C) the difference between sales and cost of sales D) sale revenue less cost of sales and expenses Answer: d Q: Which of the following expenses relate to the profit and loss account of a manufacturing firm? A) Administrative overhead. B) Direct labour C) Direct materials. D) Work-in-progress. Answer: a Q: Use the information below to answer question 39 and 40 Rakya and Joy are in partnership and agreed that 5% interest per annum is to be charged on drawings. The drawing made by both partners in one year were: Rakiya, ₦200 on March 31 and ₦300 on September 30, Joy, ₦100 on April 1 and ₦240 on July 1 The interest on Joy’s drawing is A) ₦6.00 B) ₦7.25 C) ₦9.00 D) ₦9.75 Answer: d Solution: Assuming the accounting year ends on December 31, we calculate interest on Joy’s drawings from the date of each drawing to the year-end: ₦100 drawn on April 1 Interest for 9 months (Apr 1–Dec 31): 100 × 5% × 9/12 = 100 × 0.05 × 0.75 = ₦3.75 ₦240 drawn on July 1 Interest for 6 months (Jul 1–Dec 31): 240 × 5% × 6/12 = 240 × 0.05 × 0.5 = ₦6.00 Total interest on Joy’s drawings = ₦3.75 + ₦6.00 = ₦9.75 Q: One of the reasons for the existence of the public sector is to A) take adequate care of the needy B) supplement the commercial sector C) provide cheap services to all citizens D) correct perceived inequalities. Answer: c Q: Use the information below to answer question 49 to 50. Goods worth ₦300 was transferred from department Q to P Similarly, P's total expenses for the period was ₦200 What was department Q's gross profit? A) ₦2 500 B) ₦2 300 C) ₦ 2 200 D) ₦1700 Answer: a Solution: Given (from extract): Opening stock (Q) = ₦1,000 Purchases (Q) = ₦1,500 Closing stock (Q) = ₦1,000 Sales (Q) = ₦4,000 Cost of goods sold (Q) = Opening stock + Purchases − Closing stock = 1,000 + 1,500 − 1,000 = ₦1,500 Gross profit (Q) = Sales − Cost of goods sold = 4,000 − 1,500 = ₦2,500 Q: The balance on a purchase ledger control account represents the? A) present amount that a business owes its suppliers at date B) total credit avaiable to the end of the year to be utilized in future C) total credit the business enjoyed for the particular year from its suppliers D) total credit owd the business by its customers Answer: a Solution: The balance on the purchase ledger control account represents the present amount that the business owes its suppliers at that date. Q: Companies and Allied Matters Act. 1990 requires every company to keep certain statutory books. Which of the following is not part of the statutory books to be kept by the company? A) register of directors and secretaries B) a register of charges (fixed and floating) C) minutes books of meetings of the company and meetings of its directors D) a register of companies in the same line of business Answer: d Q: ₦ Bank account 59,410 Capital account 50,000 Purchase account 20,000 Rent 2,500 Stationery 90 typewriter 6,500 Sales 38,000 In preparing a trial from the list of balances given above, what is the total in debit and credit columns? A) ₦147,910 B) ₦138,500 C) ₦88,500 D) ₦85,800 Answer: c Solution: To prepare a trial balance, classify each account as either a debit or credit balance. Debit Balances: Bank account: ₦59,410 Purchase account: ₦20,000 Rent: ₦2,500 Stationery: ₦90 Typewriter: ₦6,500 Total Debits: ₦88,500 Credit Balances: Capital account: ₦50,000 Sales: ₦38,000 Total Credits: ₦88,500 In a trial balance, the total of debit column should equal the total of credit column. Both columns total ₦88,500. Q: Which of the following is component of prime cost? A) Depreciation B) Royalty C) Factory rent D) Factory electricity Answer: d Q: Zakari started a business on January 2000. He bought a shop costing N 54,000 and stock worth N 7,600. Profit for the year amounted to N 22,100. His closing capital was N 73,800. Zakari’s personal drawings amounted to A) N 2,300 B) N9,900 C) N 17,100 D) N 19,500 Answer: b Q: A set of instructions or programs which controls the operation of a computer is A) software. B) hardware. C) monitor. D) keyboard. Answer: a Q: Which of the following is a factory overhead? A) carriage on raw materials B) Purchase of raw materials C) Production wages D) Depreciation of factory equipment. Answer: d Q: A company provided the following information about its balance sheet: Cash N100 Accounts receivable N500 Stockholders' equity 14700 Account payable N200 Bank loans Nl000 Based on the information provided, how much are Remington's liabilities? A) N200 B) N900 C) N 1,200 D) N 1,700 Answer: c Q: The capital employed is A) ₦13 000 B) ₦9 900 C) ₦8 400 D) ₦9 000 Answer: d Solution: Method 1: Owner's Equity approach Capital Employed = Capital + ₦et Profit - Drawings Capital Employed = ₦8,400 + ₦1,500 - ₦900 Capital Employed = ₦9,000 Method 2: Total Assets - Current Liabilities Total Assets = ₦4,500 + ₦3,400 + ₦2,800 + ₦2,200 + ₦100 = ₦13,000 Current Liabilities = Creditors + Accruals = ₦2,500 + ₦1,500 = ₦4,000 Capital Employed = ₦13,000 - ₦4,000 = ₦9,000 Q: Use the information below to answer this question. A business has three departments x, y and z You are given the following information Selling and distribution expenses ₦5200 Rent for the year₦6000 Department turnover floor space in square metres X ₦60,000 80 Y ₦80,000 60 Z ₦100,000 60 How much rent is apportioned to department Z? A) ₦1, 500 B) ₦3, 000 C) ₦1, 800 D) ₦2, 000 Answer: c Solution: Rent is apportioned on floor‐space. Total space = 80 + 60 + 60 = 200 m², so rent per m² = 6 000 ÷ 200 = ₦30/m². Department Z has 60 m², so its share = 60 × 30 = ₦1 800. Q: Which of the following is an item in the debit side of the sales ledger control account? A) Interest charged by suppliers B) Bills receivable honoured C) Transfer of credit balances from credit control account D) Transfer of debit balances from creditors control account Answer: a Q: The importance of bank statement is all except A) verifies the accuracy of balances of cash book and cheque book B) helps to detect and rectify any error C) helps to debit an account D) helps to update the cash book Answer: c Solution: Bank statement is prepared by the bank to an account border showing the transactions between the customer and the bank within a period of time. It is usually issued monthly or at agreed intervals to the customers. Q: In company accounts, profit after tax is shared in the A) appropriation account B) revaluation account C) current account D) realization account. Answer: a Q: In reconciling the branch and head office accounts, remittance in transit in the branch books is treated as a_____________ A) Debit entry B) Contra entry C) . Credit entry D) Reversal entry Answer: a Solution: In the branch’s own books, when cash is sent to head office but not yet received there, it isn’t left in the cash balance, instead the branch debits a “Remittance in Transit” asset account and credits cash. Thus, on reconciliation, the branch treats remittances in transit as debit entries. Q: Use the information below to answer this question. Dangote acquired Dantata’s business for ₦350,000. The total asset work were ₦820,000 and liabilities amounted to ₦ 640,000 The double entry to record the goodwill in the books is debt A) purchase of business account and credit cash account B) goodwill account and credit purchase of business account C) cash account and credit goodwill account D) goodwill account and credit cash account Answer: b Solution: when there is excess of purchase consideration over net assets, the accounting entries is to debit goodwill account as the receiving account and credit purchase of business account as the giving account. Q: The objective of allocating all costs to producer is to? A) produce a scientifically accurate cost B) avoid unallocated overhead and compute total accounts C) co-odinate the cost and financial accounts D) compute the contribution of the product to the final profit Answer: b Solution: The primary objective of allocating all costs to the product (producer) under full or absorption costing is to ensure that no overhead remains unallocated and that the total cost of production is fully captured. Q: Cash received from the subscribed shares is recorded by debting? A) application, allotment and crediting cash B) allotment and crediting cash C) cash and crediting subscribed shares D) cash, crediting application and allotment account Answer: d Solution: When cash is received from subscribed shares, the journal entry is: Debit: Cash Account (cash is coming into the company) Credit: Application and Allotment Account (to record the liability to issue shares) Q: Receipts and payments accounts is the summary of? A) income and expenditure B) cash book C) balance sheet D) profit and loss Answer: b Solution: A receipts & payments account is simply a cash summary — it records all cash and bank receipts and payments for a period (opening balance, cash in, cash out, closing balance). It’s a summary of the cash book, not an accrual statement like the income & expenditure account or a balance sheet. Q: Derive the stock turnover period.(Average stock = 23,000. Cost of sales = 300,000 year = 365 days). A) 28 days B) 42 days C) 27 days D) 23 days Answer: a Solution: Average stock / cost of sales x 365days. 23,000 ÷ 300,000 x 365 = 27.9 (Approximately 28 days) Q: At the end the fiscal year, account receivable has a balance of 100,000 and allowance for doubtful account has a balance of 7,000. The expected that realized value of the receivable is: account A) N 107,000 B) N100,000 C) c. N93,000 D) N 147,000 Answer: c Q: A bookkeeping error occurs when there is? A) a deliberate manipulation of records B) unintentional correct posting in the ledger C) intentional failure to record transactions completely D) incorrect records and oversights that are not intended Answer: d Solution: A bookkeeping error is characterized by unintended mistakes in recording transactions, such as transposition errors, omissions, or incorrect amounts, that arise from oversight or misunderstanding, rather than any deliberate action. Q: Which of the following indicate that a partnership business is in place? (i) There is a business (ii)It is run commonly by partners (iii)It has profit-making in view (iv) Partners' liability is limited A) i and ii only B) i, ii and iii only C) i, iii and iv only D) ii, iii and iv only Answer: b Solution: Essential characteristics of partnership: Carrying on a business Joint operation by partners With a view to making profit Unlimited liability (not limited) The correct indicators are (i), (ii), and (iii) only. Q: The concept which establishes the rule for the periodic recognition of revenue as soon as it is capable of objective measurement is A) going concern. B) entity. C) consistency. D) realization. Answer: d Q: In the absence of a sales day book or sales account the credit for sales can be computed from A) creditors control account B) debtors control account C) opening figures of the balance sheet D) closing figures of the balance sheet Answer: b Solution: The debtors control account (sales ledger control account) summarizes all transactions with customers. In the absence of a sales day book, you can compute total credit sales by analyzing this account because it records credit sales, receipts, returns, and discounts related to debtors. Q: The accounting method that reports incomes when earned and expenses when incurred is called? A) cash accounting B) commitment accounting C) fund accounting D) accrual accounting Answer: d Solution: Accrual accounting records income when it is earned (not necessarily when cash is received) and expenses when they are incurred (not necessarily when cash is paid). This method gives a more accurate picture of financial performance than cash accounting, which only records transactions when cash changes hands. Q: Find the salary charged to Zera product. A) N 1 854 B) N 1 845 C) N 1 062 D) N 1 134. Answer: c Q: A statement in a double-entry system in which are recorded all the transactions of one specific class, which takes place during the period is called A) Double entry system B) Ledger C) Cash Book D) Petty Cash Book Answer: b Solution: A ledger is a separate record within the general ledger that is assigned to a specific asset, liability, equity item, revenue type, or expense type. Examples of ledger accounts are: Cash, Accounts receivable.
